9011 — Al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam reported: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out during the year of al-Ḥudaybiyyah intending to visit the Sacred House, not to fight. He brought seventy sacrificial camels, while the people numbered seven hundred, so each camel was offered on behalf of ten men.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached ʿUsfān, Bishr ibn Sufyān al-Kaʿbī met him and said, “Messenger of Allah, Quraysh have heard of your approach. They have come out with nursing she-camels and their young, dressed in leopard skins and pledging before Allah that you will never enter Makkah against their will. Khālid ibn al-Walīd has been sent ahead with their cavalry to Kurāʿ al-Ghamīm.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “How unfortunate Quraysh are! War has consumed them. What harm would it do them to leave me to deal with the rest of the people? If they defeat me, that will be what they desire. But if Allah grants me victory, they may enter Islam with their strength intact. If they choose not to, they may then fight while still possessing strength. What do Quraysh imagine? By Allah, I shall continue striving against them for the cause with which Allah sent me until Allah grants me victory or this neck is severed.”
He then instructed the people to take the route to the right through al-Ḥumḍ, along a road leading to the Pass of al-Marār and al-Ḥudaybiyyah from below Makkah. He led the army along that road. When the Quraysh cavalry saw the dust raised by the army and realised that the Muslims had changed their route, they galloped back to Quraysh.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ continued until his she-camel knelt down at the Pass of al-Marār. The people said, “She has become stubborn.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “She has not become stubborn, nor is stubbornness part of her nature. Rather, she has been restrained from Makkah by the One who restrained the elephant. By Allah, Quraysh will not invite me today to any proposal involving the maintenance of kinship without my accepting it.”
He then told the people: “Dismount.” They said, “Messenger of Allah, there is no water in the valley beside which the people can camp.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took an arrow from his quiver and gave it to one of his Companions. The man descended into one of the wells and planted the arrow in it, whereupon the water surged forth until the people and their animals gathered abundantly around it.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had settled at the campsite, Budayl ibn Warqāʾ arrived with some men of Khuzāʿah. The Prophet ﷺ told them essentially what he had told Bishr ibn Sufyān. They returned to Quraysh and said, “People of Quraysh, you are acting hastily against Muḥammad. Muḥammad has not come to fight; he has come only to visit this House and honour its sanctity.” Quraysh distrusted them.
Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq reported that al-Zuhrī said: Khuzāʿah—both its polytheists and Muslims—were trusted confidants and sincere advisers of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They concealed from him nothing that occurred in Makkah.
Quraysh said, “Even if that is his sole purpose, by Allah, he will never enter Makkah against our will, lest the Arabs speak of it.”
They sent Mikraz ibn Ḥafṣ, a man of Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy, to him. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw him, he said: “This is a treacherous man.” When Mikraz reached him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave him essentially the same message he had given the previous envoys. Mikraz returned to Quraysh and conveyed the Prophet’s words.
They then sent al-Ḥulays ibn ʿAlqamah al-Kinānī, who was the leader of the allied tribes at that time. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw him, he said: “This man belongs to a people who are deeply devoted to religious observances. Send the sacrificial animals out before him.”
The animals were sent toward him, flowing across the breadth of the valley with their garlands upon them. Their hair had become worn from being detained so long from the place of sacrifice. Out of reverence for what he saw, al-Ḥulays turned back without reaching the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He told Quraysh, “I have seen something that it is not lawful to prevent: sacrificial animals wearing their garlands, their hair worn away from being detained so long from their place of sacrifice.” They replied, “Sit down. You are merely a Bedouin with no knowledge.”
They then sent ʿUrwah ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī. He said, “People of Quraysh, I have seen how harshly and abusively you treat the men whom you send to Muḥammad when they return. You know that you are like parents to me and I am like a son to you. When I heard of the difficulty that had befallen you, I gathered those of my people who obeyed me and came to support you personally.”
They replied, “You have spoken truthfully. We do not mistrust you.”
He went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, sat before him and said, “Muḥammad, you have gathered the rabble and brought them against your own family to destroy it! Quraysh have come out with nursing she-camels and their young, dressed in leopard skins and pledging before Allah that you will never enter Makkah against their will. By Allah, I can almost see these people abandoning you tomorrow.”
Abū Bakr was sitting behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, “Go suck al-Lāt’s clitoris! Would we abandon him?”
ʿUrwah asked, “Who is this, Muḥammad?”
He replied: “This is the son of Abū Quḥāfah.”
ʿUrwah said, “By Allah, were it not for a favour you once did me, I would repay your words in kind. Let that favour settle this.”
ʿUrwah then reached for the beard of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah was standing over the Prophet ﷺ in armour, and he struck ʿUrwah’s hand, saying, “Remove your hand from the beard of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ before, by Allah, it is prevented from returning to you.”
ʿUrwah said, “Woe to you! How harsh and coarse you are!” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled.
ʿUrwah asked, “Who is this, Muḥammad?”
He replied: “This is your nephew, al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah.”
ʿUrwah said, “You treacherous man! Was it not only yesterday that I settled the disgrace of your treachery?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave him the same message he had given the previous envoys and informed him that he had not come seeking war.
ʿUrwah then departed, having observed how the Prophet’s Companions treated him: whenever he performed ablution they rushed for the remaining water; whenever he spat they rushed to receive it; and whenever a hair fell from him they picked it up.
He returned to Quraysh and said, “People of Quraysh, I have visited Chosroes in his kingdom, and I have visited Caesar and the Negus in their kingdoms. By Allah, I have never seen any king among his subjects like Muḥammad among his Companions. I have seen people who will never surrender him for anything. Consider carefully what you will do.”
Before that, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had sent Khirāsh ibn Umayyah al-Khuzāʿī to Makkah, mounted upon one of his camels, to inform its chiefs of the purpose for which he had come. Quraysh hamstrung the Messenger’s camel and intended to kill Khirāsh, but the allied tribes protected him. They released him, and he returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Prophet ﷺ then summoned ʿUmar to send him to Makkah. ʿUmar said, “Messenger of Allah, I fear that Quraysh may kill me. There is no one from Banū ʿAdī in Makkah to protect me, and Quraysh know my hostility and severity toward them. But I can direct you to a man who possesses greater protection there than I do: ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned ʿUthmān and sent him to Quraysh to inform them that he had not come to fight anyone, but only to visit the Sacred House and honour its sanctity.
ʿUthmān travelled to Makkah, where Abān ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ met him. Abān dismounted, seated ʿUthmān before him on his mount and rode behind him, granting him protection until he could deliver the Messenger’s message.
ʿUthmān went to Abū Sufyān and the leading men of Quraysh and conveyed the message of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They told him, “If you wish to circumambulate the House, you may do so.”
He replied, “I would never do so before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ circumambulates it.” Quraysh detained him, and word reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that ʿUthmān had been killed.
Muḥammad reported that al-Zuhrī told him: Quraysh sent Suhayl ibn ʿAmr, of Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy, saying, “Go to Muḥammad and conclude a treaty with him, but the treaty must require him to turn back this year. By Allah, the Arabs must never be allowed to say that he entered Makkah against our will.”
When Suhayl ibn ʿAmr came, the Prophet ﷺ said: “The people now desire peace, since they have sent this man.”
When Suhayl reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they spoke at length and exchanged proposals until they agreed upon peace. When the matter had been settled and only the written document remained, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb went to Abū Bakr and asked, “Abū Bakr, is he not the Messenger of Allah? Are we not Muslims? Are they not polytheists?”
He replied, “Indeed.”
ʿUmar asked, “Why, then, should we accept humiliation in our religion?”
Abū Bakr said, “ʿUmar, hold firmly to his stirrup wherever he leads, for I testify that he is the Messenger of Allah.”
ʿUmar replied, “And I testify to that.”
ʿUmar then went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked, “Messenger of Allah, are we not Muslims? Are they not polytheists?”
He replied: “Indeed.”
ʿUmar asked, “Why, then, should we accept humiliation in our religion?”
He replied: “I am Allah’s servant and Messenger. I shall never oppose His command, and He will never abandon me.”
ʿUmar later said: “Because of what I had done and the words I had spoken that day, I continued fasting, praying, giving charity and emancipating slaves until I hoped that the matter had been turned to good.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and said: “Write: ‘In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.’”
Suhayl ibn ʿAmr said, “I do not acknowledge this. Write instead: ‘In Your name, O Allah.’”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Write: ‘In Your name, O Allah. This is the treaty concluded by Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah, with Suhayl ibn ʿAmr.’”
Suhayl said, “Had I acknowledged that you were the Messenger of Allah, I would not have fought you. Write instead: ‘This is the agreement concluded by Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh and Suhayl ibn ʿAmr.’”
They agreed to suspend warfare for ten years, during which the people would enjoy security and refrain from attacking one another. Any man of Quraysh who came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ without his guardian’s permission would be returned, whereas anyone who left the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for Quraysh would not be returned. Relations between them would be sincere and free of hidden hostility, with neither theft nor treachery.
The written conditions also stipulated that any tribe wishing to enter the alliance and covenant of Muḥammad could do so, and any tribe wishing to enter the alliance and covenant of Quraysh could do so.
Khuzāʿah immediately declared, “We enter the alliance and covenant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” Banū Bakr declared, “We enter the alliance and covenant of Quraysh.”
The treaty further stipulated: “You will turn back this year and not enter Makkah. Next year we will withdraw from the city, and you may enter it with your Companions and remain for three days. You may carry only a traveller’s weapons—swords kept in their scabbards.”
While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was having the agreement written, Abū Jandal ibn Suhayl ibn ʿAmr arrived in chains, having escaped to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Companions had set out with no doubt that victory would occur because of a vision the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had seen. When they witnessed the treaty, the return without entering Makkah and the concessions the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had accepted, they were overwhelmed by such distress that they nearly perished from grief.
When Suhayl saw Abū Jandal, he went to him, struck him in the face and said, “Muḥammad, our agreement was concluded before this man came to you.”
The Prophet ﷺ said: “You have spoken truthfully.”
Suhayl seized Abū Jandal by the front of his clothing. Abū Jandal cried out at the top of his voice, “Muslims! Will you return me to the polytheists so that they may persecute me for my religion?” This only intensified the people’s anguish.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Abū Jandal, remain patient and seek your reward from Allah. Allah will provide relief and a way out for you and the other oppressed Muslims with you. We have concluded a treaty with these people, giving them our covenant and receiving theirs in return. We will not betray them.”
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb went to Abū Jandal and walked beside him, saying, “Be patient, Abū Jandal. They are only polytheists, and the blood of any one of them is merely the blood of a dog.” ʿUmar brought the sword’s hilt close to him, hoping that he would seize it and strike his father, but Abū Jandal could not bring himself to kill his father.
The agreement was carried into effect. When they had finished writing it—the Messenger of Allah ﷺ praying within the sacred precinct while his camp stood outside it—he arose and said: “People, slaughter your sacrificial animals and shave your heads.” No one stood.
He repeated the command, but no one stood. He repeated it a third time, yet still no one rose.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the tent of Umm Salamah and asked: “Umm Salamah, what is the matter with the people?”
She replied, “Messenger of Allah, they have been overwhelmed by the grief you have seen. Do not speak to any of them. Go directly to your sacrificial animal, slaughter it and shave your head. Once you have done so, the people will follow.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out without speaking to anyone. He approached his sacrificial animal and slaughtered it, then sat down and had his head shaved. The people immediately arose, slaughtered their animals and shaved their heads.
When they reached the middle of the road between Makkah and Madinah, Sūrat al-Fatḥ was revealed.
Good: Related by Imām Aḥmad (18910) and Ibn Hishām in al-Sīrah (2/308). Some passages in Ibn Isḥāq’s account are open to question, including the statement that the people numbered seven hundred, as explained shortly before.

He told Quraysh, “I have seen something that it is not lawful to prevent: sacrificial animals wearing their garlands, their hair worn away from being detained so long from their place of sacrifice.” They replied, “Sit down. You are merely a Bedouin with no knowledge.”
They then sent ʿUrwah ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī. He said, “People of Quraysh, I have seen how harshly and abusively you treat the men whom you send to Muḥammad when they return. You know that you are like parents to me and I am like a son to you. When I heard of the difficulty that had befallen you, I gathered those of my people who obeyed me and came to support you personally.”
They replied, “You have spoken truthfully. We do not mistrust you.”
He went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, sat before him and said, “Muḥammad, you have gathered the rabble and brought them against your own family to destroy it! Quraysh have come out with nursing she-camels and their young, dressed in leopard skins and pledging before Allah that you will never enter Makkah against their will. By Allah, I can almost see these people abandoning you tomorrow.”
Abū Bakr was sitting behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, “Go suck al-Lāt’s clitoris! Would we abandon him?”
ʿUrwah asked, “Who is this, Muḥammad?”
He replied: “This is the son of Abū Quḥāfah.”
ʿUrwah said, “By Allah, were it not for a favour you once did me, I would repay your words in kind. Let that favour settle this.”
ʿUrwah then reached for the beard of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah was standing over the Prophet ﷺ in armour, and he struck ʿUrwah’s hand, saying, “Remove your hand from the beard of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ before, by Allah, it is prevented from returning to you.”
ʿUrwah said, “Woe to you! How harsh and coarse you are!” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled.
ʿUrwah asked, “Who is this, Muḥammad?”
He replied: “This is your nephew, al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah.”
ʿUrwah said, “You treacherous man! Was it not only yesterday that I settled the disgrace of your treachery?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave him the same message he had given the previous envoys and informed him that he had not come seeking war.
ʿUrwah then departed, having observed how the Prophet’s Companions treated him: whenever he performed ablution they rushed for the remaining water; whenever he spat they rushed to receive it; and whenever a hair fell from him they picked it up.
He returned to Quraysh and said, “People of Quraysh, I have visited Chosroes in his kingdom, and I have visited Caesar and the Negus in their kingdoms. By Allah, I have never seen any king among his subjects like Muḥammad among his Companions. I have seen people who will never surrender him for anything. Consider carefully what you will do.”
Before that, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had sent Khirāsh ibn Umayyah al-Khuzāʿī to Makkah, mounted upon one of his camels, to inform its chiefs of the purpose for which he had come. Quraysh hamstrung the Messenger’s camel and intended to kill Khirāsh, but the allied tribes protected him. They released him, and he returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Prophet ﷺ then summoned ʿUmar to send him to Makkah. ʿUmar said, “Messenger of Allah, I fear that Quraysh may kill me. There is no one from Banū ʿAdī in Makkah to protect me, and Quraysh know my hostility and severity toward them. But I can direct you to a man who possesses greater protection there than I do: ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned ʿUthmān and sent him to Quraysh to inform them that he had not come to fight anyone, but only to visit the Sacred House and honour its sanctity.
ʿUthmān travelled to Makkah, where Abān ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ met him. Abān dismounted, seated ʿUthmān before him on his mount and rode behind him, granting him protection until he could deliver the Messenger’s message.
ʿUthmān went to Abū Sufyān and the leading men of Quraysh and conveyed the message of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They told him, “If you wish to circumambulate the House, you may do so.”
He replied, “I would never do so before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ circumambulates it.” Quraysh detained him, and word reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that ʿUthmān had been killed.
Muḥammad reported that al-Zuhrī told him: Quraysh sent Suhayl ibn ʿAmr, of Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy, saying, “Go to Muḥammad and conclude a treaty with him, but the treaty must require him to turn back this year. By Allah, the Arabs must never be allowed to say that he entered Makkah against our will.”
When Suhayl ibn ʿAmr came, the Prophet ﷺ said: “The people now desire peace, since they have sent this man.”
When Suhayl reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they spoke at length and exchanged proposals until they agreed upon peace. When the matter had been settled and only the written document remained, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb went to Abū Bakr and asked, “Abū Bakr, is he not the Messenger of Allah? Are we not Muslims? Are they not polytheists?”
He replied, “Indeed.”
ʿUmar asked, “Why, then, should we accept humiliation in our religion?”
Abū Bakr said, “ʿUmar, hold firmly to his stirrup wherever he leads, for I testify that he is the Messenger of Allah.”
ʿUmar replied, “And I testify to that.”
ʿUmar then went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked, “Messenger of Allah, are we not Muslims? Are they not polytheists?”
He replied: “Indeed.”
ʿUmar asked, “Why, then, should we accept humiliation in our religion?”
He replied: “I am Allah’s servant and Messenger. I shall never oppose His command, and He will never abandon me.”
ʿUmar later said: “Because of what I had done and the words I had spoken that day, I continued fasting, praying, giving charity and emancipating slaves until I hoped that the matter had been turned to good.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and said: “Write: ‘In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.’”
Suhayl ibn ʿAmr said, “I do not acknowledge this. Write instead: ‘In Your name, O Allah.’”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Write: ‘In Your name, O Allah. This is the treaty concluded by Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah, with Suhayl ibn ʿAmr.’”
Suhayl said, “Had I acknowledged that you were the Messenger of Allah, I would not have fought you. Write instead: ‘This is the agreement concluded by Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh and Suhayl ibn ʿAmr.’”
They agreed to suspend warfare for ten years, during which the people would enjoy security and refrain from attacking one another. Any man of Quraysh who came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ without his guardian’s permission would be returned, whereas anyone who left the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for Quraysh would not be returned. Relations between them would be sincere and free of hidden hostility, with neither theft nor treachery.
The written conditions also stipulated that any tribe wishing to enter the alliance and covenant of Muḥammad could do so, and any tribe wishing to enter the alliance and covenant of Quraysh could do so.
Khuzāʿah immediately declared, “We enter the alliance and covenant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” Banū Bakr declared, “We enter the alliance and covenant of Quraysh.”
The treaty further stipulated: “You will turn back this year and not enter Makkah. Next year we will withdraw from the city, and you may enter it with your Companions and remain for three days. You may carry only a traveller’s weapons—swords kept in their scabbards.”
While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was having the agreement written, Abū Jandal ibn Suhayl ibn ʿAmr arrived in chains, having escaped to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Companions had set out with no doubt that victory would occur because of a vision the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had seen. When they witnessed the treaty, the return without entering Makkah and the concessions the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had accepted, they were overwhelmed by such distress that they nearly perished from grief.
When Suhayl saw Abū Jandal, he went to him, struck him in the face and said, “Muḥammad, our agreement was concluded before this man came to you.”
The Prophet ﷺ said: “You have spoken truthfully.”
Suhayl seized Abū Jandal by the front of his clothing. Abū Jandal cried out at the top of his voice, “Muslims! Will you return me to the polytheists so that they may persecute me for my religion?” This only intensified the people’s anguish.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Abū Jandal, remain patient and seek your reward from Allah. Allah will provide relief and a way out for you and the other oppressed Muslims with you. We have concluded a treaty with these people, giving them our covenant and receiving theirs in return. We will not betray them.”
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb went to Abū Jandal and walked beside him, saying, “Be patient, Abū Jandal. They are only polytheists, and the blood of any one of them is merely the blood of a dog.” ʿUmar brought the sword’s hilt close to him, hoping that he would seize it and strike his father, but Abū Jandal could not bring himself to kill his father.
The agreement was carried into effect. When they had finished writing it—the Messenger of Allah ﷺ praying within the sacred precinct while his camp stood outside it—he arose and said: “People, slaughter your sacrificial animals and shave your heads.” No one stood.
He repeated the command, but no one stood. He repeated it a third time, yet still no one rose.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the tent of Umm Salamah and asked: “Umm Salamah, what is the matter with the people?”
She replied, “Messenger of Allah, they have been overwhelmed by the grief you have seen. Do not speak to any of them. Go directly to your sacrificial animal, slaughter it and shave your head. Once you have done so, the people will follow.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out without speaking to anyone. He approached his sacrificial animal and slaughtered it, then sat down and had his head shaved. The people immediately arose, slaughtered their animals and shaved their heads.
When they reached the middle of the road between Makkah and Madinah, Sūrat al-Fatḥ was revealed.
Good: Related by Imām Aḥmad (18910) and Ibn Hishām in al-Sīrah (2/308). Some passages in Ibn Isḥāq’s account are open to question, including the statement that the people numbered seven hundred, as explained shortly before.

٩٠١١ — عن المسور بن مخرمة ومروان بن الحكم قالا: خرج رسول الله ﷺ عام الحديبية يريد زيارة البيت، لا يريد قتالًا، وساق معه الهدي سبعين بدنة، وكان الناس سبعمائة رجل، فكانت كل بدنة عن عشرة.
وخرج رسول الله ﷺ حتى إذا كان بعسفان لقيه بشر بن سفيان الكعبي، فقال: يا رسول الله، هذه قريش قد سمعت بمسيرك، فخرجت معها العوذ المطافيل، قد لبسوا جلود النمور، يعاهدون الله ألا تدخلها عليهم عنوة أبدًا، وهذا خالد بن الوليد في خيلهم قد قدموه إلى كراع الغميم.
فقال رسول الله ﷺ: «يَا وَيْحَ قُرَيْشٍ! لَقَدْ أَكَلَتْهُمُ الْحَرْبُ، مَاذَا عَلَيْهِمْ لَوْ خَلَّوْا بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ سَائِرِ النَّاسِ؟ فَإِنْ أَصَابُونِي كَانَ الَّذِي أَرَادُوا، وَإِنْ أَظْهَرَنِي اللهُ عَلَيْهِمْ دَخَلُوا فِي الْإِسْلَامِ وَهُمْ وَافِرُونَ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَفْعَلُوا قَاتَلُوا وَبِهِمْ قُوَّةٌ. فَمَاذَا تَظُنُّ قُرَيْشٌ؟ فَوَاللهِ لَا أَزَالُ أُجَاهِدُهُمْ عَلَى الَّذِي بَعَثَنِي اللهُ بِهِ حَتَّى يُظْهِرَنِي اللهُ، أَوْ تَنْفَرِدَ هَذِهِ السَّالِفَةُ».
ثم أمر الناس فسلكوا ذات اليمين بين ظهري الحمض، على طريق تخرجه على ثنية المرار والحديبية من أسفل مكة. قال: فسلك بالجيش تلك الطريق، فلما رأت خيل قريش قترة الجيش، وقد خالفوا عن طريقهم، ركضوا راجعين إلى قريش.
فخرج رسول الله ﷺ حتى إذا سلك ثنية المرار بركت ناقته، فقال الناس: خلأت. فقال رسول الله ﷺ: «مَا خَلَأَتْ، وَمَا هُوَ لَهَا بِخُلُقٍ، وَلَكِنْ حَبَسَهَا حَابِسُ الْفِيلِ عَنْ مَكَّةَ. وَاللهِ لَا تَدْعُونِي قُرَيْشٌ الْيَوْمَ إِلَى خُطَّةٍ يَسْأَلُونَنِي فِيهَا صِلَةَ الرَّحِمِ إِلَّا أَعْطَيْتُهُمْ إِيَّاهَا».
ثم قال للناس: «انْزِلُوا». فقالوا: يا رسول الله، ما بالوادي من ماء ينزل عليه الناس. فأخرج رسول الله ﷺ سهمًا من كنانته، فأعطاه رجلًا من أصحابه، فنزل في قليب من تلك القُلُب، فغرزه فيه، فجاش الماء حتى ضرب الناس عنه بعطن.
فلما اطمأن رسول الله ﷺ إذا بديل بن ورقاء في رجال من خزاعة، فقال لهم كقوله لبشر بن سفيان. فرجعوا إلى قريش فقالوا: يا معشر قريش، إنكم تعجلون على محمد، وإن محمدًا لم يأت لقتال، إنما جاء زائرًا لهذا البيت، معظمًا لحقه. فاتهموهم.
قال محمد بن إسحاق: قال الزهري: وكانت خزاعة عَيْبَةَ نُصْحِ رسول الله ﷺ، مشركها ومسلمها، لا يخفون على رسول الله ﷺ شيئًا كان بمكة.
فقالوا: وإن كان إنما جاء لذلك، فوالله لا يدخلها أبدًا علينا عنوة، ولا تتحدث بذلك العرب.
ثم بعثوا إليه مكرز بن حفص، أحد بني عامر بن لؤي. فلما رآه رسول الله ﷺ قال: «هَذَا رَجُلٌ غَادِرٌ». فلما انتهى إلى رسول الله ﷺ كلّمه رسول الله ﷺ بنحو ما كلم به أصحابه، ثم رجع إلى قريش فأخبرهم بما قال له رسول الله ﷺ.
قال: فبعثوا إليه الحليس بن علقمة الكناني، وهو يومئذ سيد الأحابيش. فلما رآه رسول الله ﷺ قال: «هَذَا مِنْ قَوْمٍ يَتَأَلَّهُونَ، فَابْعَثُوا الْهَدْيَ فِي وَجْهِهِ».
فبعثوا الهدي، فلما رأى الهدي يسيل عليه من عرض الوادي في قلائده، قد أكل أوباره من طول الحبس عن محله، رجع ولم يصل إلى رسول الله ﷺ إعظامًا لما رأى. فقال: يا معشر قريش، قد رأيت ما لا يحل صده: الهدي في قلائده، قد أكل أوباره من طول الحبس عن محله. قالوا: اجلس، إنما أنت أعرابي لا علم لك.
فبعثوا إليه عروة بن مسعود الثقفي، فقال: يا معشر قريش، إني قد رأيت ما يلقى منكم من تبعثون إلى محمد إذا جاءكم من التعنيف وسوء اللفظ، وقد عرفتم أنكم والد وأني ولد، وقد سمعت بالذي نابكم، فجمعت من أطاعني من قومي، ثم جئت حتى آسيتكم بنفسي. قالوا: صدقت، ما أنت عندنا بمتهم.
فخرج حتى أتى رسول الله ﷺ، فجلس بين يديه، فقال: يا محمد، جمعت أوباش الناس، ثم جئت بهم لبيضتك تفضها! إنها قريش قد خرجت معها العوذ المطافيل، قد لبسوا جلود النمور، يعاهدون الله ألا تدخلها عليهم عنوة أبدًا. وأيم الله، لكأني بهؤلاء قد انكشفوا عنك غدًا.
قال: وأبو بكر قاعد خلف رسول الله ﷺ، فقال: امصص بظر اللات! أنحن ننكشف عنه؟ فقال: من هذا يا محمد؟ قال: «هَذَا ابْنُ أَبِي قُحَافَةَ». قال: أما والله لولا يد كانت لك عندي لكافأتك بها، ولكن هذه بها.
ثم تناول لحية رسول الله ﷺ، والمغيرة بن شعبة واقف على رأس رسول الله ﷺ في الحديد، فقرع يده، ثم قال: أمسك يدك عن لحية رسول الله ﷺ قبل، والله، لا تصل إليك.
قال: ويحك! ما أفظك وأغلظك! فتبسم رسول الله ﷺ. فقال عروة: من هذا يا محمد؟ قال: «هَذَا ابْنُ أَخِيكَ الْمُغِيرَةُ بْنُ شُعْبَةَ». قال: أي غُدَرُ، وهل غسلت سوأتك إلا بالأمس؟
قال: فكلمه رسول الله ﷺ بمثل ما كلم به أصحابه، وأخبره أنه لم يأت يريد حربًا.
فقام من عند رسول الله ﷺ، وقد رأى ما يصنع به أصحابه: لا يتوضأ وضوءًا إلا ابتدروه، ولا يبصق بصاقًا إلا ابتدروه، ولا يسقط من شعره شيء إلا أخذوه.
فرجع إلى قريش فقال: يا معشر قريش، إني جئت كسرى في ملكه، وجئت قيصر والنجاشي في ملكهما. والله ما رأيت ملكًا قط مثل محمد في أصحابه، ولقد رأيت قومًا لا يسلمونه لشيء أبدًا، فروا رأيكم.
قال: وكان رسول الله ﷺ قبل ذلك قد بعث خراش بن أمية الخزاعي إلى مكة، وحمله على جمل له، ليبلغ أشرافهم عنه ما جاء له. فعقروا به جمل رسول الله ﷺ، وأرادوا قتله، فمنعته الأحابيش، فخلوا سبيله حتى أتى رسول الله ﷺ.
فدعا عمر ليبعثه إلى مكة، فقال: يا رسول الله، إني أخاف قريشًا على نفسي، وليس بها من بني عدي أحد يمنعني، وقد عرفت قريش عداوتي إياها وغلظتي عليها، ولكن أدلك على رجل هو أعز مني: عثمان بن عفان.
قال: فدعاه رسول الله ﷺ، فبعثه إلى قريش يخبرهم أنه لم يأت لحرب أحد، وإنما جاء زائرًا لهذا البيت، معظمًا لحرمته.
فخرج عثمان حتى أتى مكة، فلقيه أبان بن سعيد بن العاص، فنزل عن دابته وحمله بين يديه، وردف خلفه، وأجاره حتى بلغ رسالة رسول الله ﷺ.
فانطلق عثمان حتى أتى أبا سفيان وعظماء قريش، فبلغهم عن رسول الله ﷺ ما أرسله به. فقالوا لعثمان: إن شئت أن تطوف بالبيت فطف به. فقال: ما كنت لأفعل حتى يطوف به رسول الله ﷺ. قال: واحتبسته قريش عندها، وبلغ رسول الله ﷺ أن عثمان قد قتل.
قال محمد: فحدثني الزهري أن قريشًا بعثوا سهيل بن عمرو، أحد بني عامر بن لؤي، وقالوا: ائت محمدًا فصالحه، ولا يكن في صلحه إلا أن يرجع عنا عامه هذا، فوالله لا تتحدث العرب أنه دخلها علينا عنوة أبدًا.
فأتاه سهيل بن عمرو، فلما رآه النبي ﷺ قال: «قَدْ أَرَادَ الْقَوْمُ الصُّلْحَ حِينَ بَعَثُوا هَذَا الرَّجُلَ».
فلما انتهى إلى رسول الله ﷺ تكلما وأطالا الكلام، وتراجعا حتى جرى بينهما الصلح. فلما التأم الأمر ولم يبق إلا الكتاب، وثب عمر بن الخطاب فأتى أبا بكر، فقال: يا أبا بكر، أوليس برسول الله؟ أولسنا بالمسلمين؟ أوليسوا بالمشركين؟ قال: بلى. قال: فعلام نعطي الذلة في ديننا؟
فقال أبو بكر: يا عمر، الزم غرزه حيث كان، فإني أشهد أنه رسول الله. قال عمر: وأنا أشهد.
ثم أتى رسول الله ﷺ فقال: يا رسول الله، أولسنا بالمسلمين؟ أوليسوا بالمشركين؟ قال: «بَلَى». قال: فعلام نعطي الذلة في ديننا؟
فقال: «أَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ وَرَسُولُهُ، لَنْ أُخَالِفَ أَمْرَهُ، وَلَنْ يُضَيِّعَنِي».
ثم قال عمر: ما زلت أصوم وأصلي وأتصدق وأعتق من الذي صنعت، مخافة كلامي الذي تكلمت به يومئذ، حتى رجوت أن يكون خيرًا.
قال: ودعا رسول الله ﷺ علي بن أبي طالب فقال: «اكْتُبْ: بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ». فقال سهيل بن عمرو: لا أعرف هذا، ولكن اكتب: باسمك اللهم.
فقال رسول الله ﷺ: «اكْتُبْ: بِاسْمِكَ اللَّهُمَّ. هَذَا مَا صَالَحَ عَلَيْهِ مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اللهِ سُهَيْلَ بْنَ عَمْرٍو».
فقال: لو شهدت أنك رسول الله لم أقاتلك، ولكن اكتب: هذا ما اصطلح عليه محمد بن عبد الله وسهيل بن عمرو.
على وضع الحرب عشر سنين، يأمن فيهن الناس، ويكف بعضهم عن بعض؛ على أنه من أتى رسول الله ﷺ من أصحابه بغير إذن وليه رده عليهم، ومن أتى قريشًا ممن مع رسول الله ﷺ لم يردوه عليه؛ وأن بيننا عَيْبَةً مَكْفُوفَةً؛ وأنه لا إسلال ولا إغلال.
وكان في شرطهم حين كتبوا الكتاب: أنه من أحب أن يدخل في عقد محمد وعهده دخل فيه، ومن أحب أن يدخل في عقد قريش وعهدهم دخل فيه.
فتواثبت خزاعة فقالوا: نحن في عقد رسول الله ﷺ وعهده. وتواثبت بنو بكر فقالوا: نحن في عقد قريش وعهدهم.
وأنك ترجع عنا عامنا هذا فلا تدخل علينا مكة، وأنه إذا كان عام قابل خرجنا عنك، فتدخلها بأصحابك، وأقمت فيهم ثلاثًا، معك سلاح الراكب، لا تدخلها بغير السيوف في القرب.
فبينما رسول الله ﷺ يكتب الكتاب إذا جاءه أبو جندل بن سهيل بن عمرو في الحديد، قد انفلت إلى رسول الله ﷺ.
قال: وقد كان أصحاب رسول الله ﷺ خرجوا وهم لا يشكون في الفتح، لرؤيا رآها رسول الله ﷺ. فلما رأوا ما رأوا من الصلح والرجوع، وما تحمل رسول الله ﷺ على نفسه، دخل الناس من ذلك أمر عظيم، حتى كادوا أن يهلكوا.
فلما رأى سهيل أبا جندل قام إليه فضرب وجهه وقال: يا محمد، قد لجت القضية بيني وبينك قبل أن يأتيك هذا. قال: «صَدَقْتَ». فقام إليه فأخذ بتلابيبه.
قال: وصرخ أبو جندل بأعلى صوته: يا معشر المسلمين، أتردونني إلى أهل الشرك فيفتنوني في ديني؟ قال: فزاد الناس شرًّا إلى ما بهم.
فقال رسول الله ﷺ: «يَا أَبَا جَنْدَلٍ، اصْبِرْ وَاحْتَسِبْ؛ فَإِنَّ اللهَ جَاعِلٌ لَكَ وَلِمَنْ مَعَكَ مِنَ الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ فَرَجًا وَمَخْرَجًا. إِنَّا قَدْ عَقَدْنَا بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ الْقَوْمِ صُلْحًا، فَأَعْطَيْنَاهُمْ عَلَى ذَلِكَ وَأَعْطَوْنَا عَلَيْهِ عَهْدًا، وَإِنَّا لَنْ نَغْدِرَ بِهِمْ».
قال: فوثب إليه عمر بن الخطاب، فجعل يمشي مع أبي جندل إلى جنبه، وهو يقول: اصبر يا أبا جندل، فإنما هم المشركون، وإنما دم أحدهم دم كلب. قال: ويدني قائم السيف منه. قال عمر: رجوت أن يأخذ السيف فيضرب به أباه. قال: فضن الرجل بأبيه.
قال: ونفذت القضية. فلما فرغا من الكتاب، وكان رسول الله ﷺ يصلي في الحرم وهو مضطرب في الحل، قام رسول الله ﷺ فقال: «يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ، انْحَرُوا وَاحْلِقُوا». قال: فما قام أحد.
قال: ثم عاد بمثلها، فما قام رجل، حتى عاد ﷺ بمثلها، فما قام رجل.
فرجع رسول الله ﷺ فدخل على أم سلمة فقال: «يَا أُمَّ سَلَمَةَ، مَا شَأْنُ النَّاسِ؟». قالت: يا رسول الله، قد دخلهم ما رأيت، فلا تكلمن منهم إنسانًا، واعمد إلى هديك حيث كان فانحره واحلق، فلو قد فعلت ذلك فعل الناس ذلك.
فخرج رسول الله ﷺ لا يكلم أحدًا، حتى أتى هديه فنحره، ثم جلس فحلق. قال: فقام الناس ينحرون ويحلقون.
قال: حتى إذا كان بين مكة والمدينة في وسط الطريق نزلت سورة الفتح.
حسن: رواه الإمام أحمد (١٨٩١٠)، وابن هشام في «السيرة» (٣٠٨/٢). لكن في بعض فقرات حديث ابن إسحاق نظر، منها قوله: «وكان الناس سبعمائة»، كما سبق بيانه قريبًا.
9011 — Al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam reported: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out during the year of al-Ḥudaybiyyah intending to visit the Sacred House, not to fight. He brought seventy sacrificial camels, while the people numbered seven hundred, so each camel was offered on behalf of ten men.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached ʿUsfān, Bishr ibn Sufyān al-Kaʿbī met him and said, “Messenger of Allah, Quraysh have heard of your approach. They have come out with nursing she-camels and their young, dressed in leopard skins and pledging before Allah that you will never enter Makkah against their will. Khālid ibn al-Walīd has been sent ahead with their cavalry to Kurāʿ al-Ghamīm.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “How unfortunate Quraysh are! War has consumed them. What harm would it do them to leave me to deal with the rest of the people? If they defeat me, that will be what they desire. But if Allah grants me victory, they may enter Islam with their strength intact. If they choose not to, they may then fight while still possessing strength. What do Quraysh imagine? By Allah, I shall continue striving against them for the cause with which Allah sent me until Allah grants me victory or this neck is severed.”
He then instructed the people to take the route to the right through al-Ḥumḍ, along a road leading to the Pass of al-Marār and al-Ḥudaybiyyah from below Makkah. He led the army along that road. When the Quraysh cavalry saw the dust raised by the army and realised that the Muslims had changed their route, they galloped back to Quraysh.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ continued until his she-camel knelt down at the Pass of al-Marār. The people said, “She has become stubborn.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “She has not become stubborn, nor is stubbornness part of her nature. Rather, she has been restrained from Makkah by the One who restrained the elephant. By Allah, Quraysh will not invite me today to any proposal involving the maintenance of kinship without my accepting it.”
He then told the people: “Dismount.” They said, “Messenger of Allah, there is no water in the valley beside which the people can camp.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took an arrow from his quiver and gave it to one of his Companions. The man descended into one of the wells and planted the arrow in it, whereupon the water surged forth until the people and their animals gathered abundantly around it.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had settled at the campsite, Budayl ibn Warqāʾ arrived with some men of Khuzāʿah. The Prophet ﷺ told them essentially what he had told Bishr ibn Sufyān. They returned to Quraysh and said, “People of Quraysh, you are acting hastily against Muḥammad. Muḥammad has not come to fight; he has come only to visit this House and honour its sanctity.” Quraysh distrusted them.
Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq reported that al-Zuhrī said: Khuzāʿah—both its polytheists and Muslims—were trusted confidants and sincere advisers of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They concealed from him nothing that occurred in Makkah.
Quraysh said, “Even if that is his sole purpose, by Allah, he will never enter Makkah against our will, lest the Arabs speak of it.”
They sent Mikraz ibn Ḥafṣ, a man of Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy, to him. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw him, he said: “This is a treacherous man.” When Mikraz reached him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave him essentially the same message he had given the previous envoys. Mikraz returned to Quraysh and conveyed the Prophet’s words.
They then sent al-Ḥulays ibn ʿAlqamah al-Kinānī, who was the leader of the allied tribes at that time. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw him, he said: “This man belongs to a people who are deeply devoted to religious observances. Send the sacrificial animals out before him.”
The animals were sent toward him, flowing across the breadth of the valley with their garlands upon them. Their hair had become worn from being detained so long from the place of sacrifice. Out of reverence for what he saw, al-Ḥulays turned back without reaching the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He told Quraysh, “I have seen something that it is not lawful to prevent: sacrificial animals wearing their garlands, their hair worn away from being detained so long from their place of sacrifice.” They replied, “Sit down. You are merely a Bedouin with no knowledge.”
They then sent ʿUrwah ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī. He said, “People of Quraysh, I have seen how harshly and abusively you treat the men whom you send to Muḥammad when they return. You know that you are like parents to me and I am like a son to you. When I heard of the difficulty that had befallen you, I gathered those of my people who obeyed me and came to support you personally.”
They replied, “You have spoken truthfully. We do not mistrust you.”
He went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, sat before him and said, “Muḥammad, you have gathered the rabble and brought them against your own family to destroy it! Quraysh have come out with nursing she-camels and their young, dressed in leopard skins and pledging before Allah that you will never enter Makkah against their will. By Allah, I can almost see these people abandoning you tomorrow.”
Abū Bakr was sitting behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, “Go suck al-Lāt’s clitoris! Would we abandon him?”
ʿUrwah asked, “Who is this, Muḥammad?”
He replied: “This is the son of Abū Quḥāfah.”
ʿUrwah said, “By Allah, were it not for a favour you once did me, I would repay your words in kind. Let that favour settle this.”
ʿUrwah then reached for the beard of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah was standing over the Prophet ﷺ in armour, and he struck ʿUrwah’s hand, saying, “Remove your hand from the beard of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ before, by Allah, it is prevented from returning to you.”
ʿUrwah said, “Woe to you! How harsh and coarse you are!” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled.
ʿUrwah asked, “Who is this, Muḥammad?”
He replied: “This is your nephew, al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah.”
ʿUrwah said, “You treacherous man! Was it not only yesterday that I settled the disgrace of your treachery?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave him the same message he had given the previous envoys and informed him that he had not come seeking war.
ʿUrwah then departed, having observed how the Prophet’s Companions treated him: whenever he performed ablution they rushed for the remaining water; whenever he spat they rushed to receive it; and whenever a hair fell from him they picked it up.
He returned to Quraysh and said, “People of Quraysh, I have visited Chosroes in his kingdom, and I have visited Caesar and the Negus in their kingdoms. By Allah, I have never seen any king among his subjects like Muḥammad among his Companions. I have seen people who will never surrender him for anything. Consider carefully what you will do.”
Before that, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had sent Khirāsh ibn Umayyah al-Khuzāʿī to Makkah, mounted upon one of his camels, to inform its chiefs of the purpose for which he had come. Quraysh hamstrung the Messenger’s camel and intended to kill Khirāsh, but the allied tribes protected him. They released him, and he returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Prophet ﷺ then summoned ʿUmar to send him to Makkah. ʿUmar said, “Messenger of Allah, I fear that Quraysh may kill me. There is no one from Banū ʿAdī in Makkah to protect me, and Quraysh know my hostility and severity toward them. But I can direct you to a man who possesses greater protection there than I do: ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned ʿUthmān and sent him to Quraysh to inform them that he had not come to fight anyone, but only to visit the Sacred House and honour its sanctity.
ʿUthmān travelled to Makkah, where Abān ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ met him. Abān dismounted, seated ʿUthmān before him on his mount and rode behind him, granting him protection until he could deliver the Messenger’s message.
ʿUthmān went to Abū Sufyān and the leading men of Quraysh and conveyed the message of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They told him, “If you wish to circumambulate the House, you may do so.”
He replied, “I would never do so before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ circumambulates it.” Quraysh detained him, and word reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that ʿUthmān had been killed.
Muḥammad reported that al-Zuhrī told him: Quraysh sent Suhayl ibn ʿAmr, of Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy, saying, “Go to Muḥammad and conclude a treaty with him, but the treaty must require him to turn back this year. By Allah, the Arabs must never be allowed to say that he entered Makkah against our will.”
When Suhayl ibn ʿAmr came, the Prophet ﷺ said: “The people now desire peace, since they have sent this man.”
When Suhayl reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they spoke at length and exchanged proposals until they agreed upon peace. When the matter had been settled and only the written document remained, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb went to Abū Bakr and asked, “Abū Bakr, is he not the Messenger of Allah? Are we not Muslims? Are they not polytheists?”
He replied, “Indeed.”
ʿUmar asked, “Why, then, should we accept humiliation in our religion?”
Abū Bakr said, “ʿUmar, hold firmly to his stirrup wherever he leads, for I testify that he is the Messenger of Allah.”
ʿUmar replied, “And I testify to that.”
ʿUmar then went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked, “Messenger of Allah, are we not Muslims? Are they not polytheists?”
He replied: “Indeed.”
ʿUmar asked, “Why, then, should we accept humiliation in our religion?”
He replied: “I am Allah’s servant and Messenger. I shall never oppose His command, and He will never abandon me.”
ʿUmar later said: “Because of what I had done and the words I had spoken that day, I continued fasting, praying, giving charity and emancipating slaves until I hoped that the matter had been turned to good.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and said: “Write: ‘In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.’”
Suhayl ibn ʿAmr said, “I do not acknowledge this. Write instead: ‘In Your name, O Allah.’”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Write: ‘In Your name, O Allah. This is the treaty concluded by Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah, with Suhayl ibn ʿAmr.’”
Suhayl said, “Had I acknowledged that you were the Messenger of Allah, I would not have fought you. Write instead: ‘This is the agreement concluded by Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh and Suhayl ibn ʿAmr.’”
They agreed to suspend warfare for ten years, during which the people would enjoy security and refrain from attacking one another. Any man of Quraysh who came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ without his guardian’s permission would be returned, whereas anyone who left the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for Quraysh would not be returned. Relations between them would be sincere and free of hidden hostility, with neither theft nor treachery.
The written conditions also stipulated that any tribe wishing to enter the alliance and covenant of Muḥammad could do so, and any tribe wishing to enter the alliance and covenant of Quraysh could do so.
Khuzāʿah immediately declared, “We enter the alliance and covenant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” Banū Bakr declared, “We enter the alliance and covenant of Quraysh.”
The treaty further stipulated: “You will turn back this year and not enter Makkah. Next year we will withdraw from the city, and you may enter it with your Companions and remain for three days. You may carry only a traveller’s weapons—swords kept in their scabbards.”
While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was having the agreement written, Abū Jandal ibn Suhayl ibn ʿAmr arrived in chains, having escaped to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Companions had set out with no doubt that victory would occur because of a vision the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had seen. When they witnessed the treaty, the return without entering Makkah and the concessions the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had accepted, they were overwhelmed by such distress that they nearly perished from grief.
When Suhayl saw Abū Jandal, he went to him, struck him in the face and said, “Muḥammad, our agreement was concluded before this man came to you.”
The Prophet ﷺ said: “You have spoken truthfully.”
Suhayl seized Abū Jandal by the front of his clothing. Abū Jandal cried out at the top of his voice, “Muslims! Will you return me to the polytheists so that they may persecute me for my religion?” This only intensified the people’s anguish.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Abū Jandal, remain patient and seek your reward from Allah. Allah will provide relief and a way out for you and the other oppressed Muslims with you. We have concluded a treaty with these people, giving them our covenant and receiving theirs in return. We will not betray them.”
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb went to Abū Jandal and walked beside him, saying, “Be patient, Abū Jandal. They are only polytheists, and the blood of any one of them is merely the blood of a dog.” ʿUmar brought the sword’s hilt close to him, hoping that he would seize it and strike his father, but Abū Jandal could not bring himself to kill his father.
The agreement was carried into effect. When they had finished writing it—the Messenger of Allah ﷺ praying within the sacred precinct while his camp stood outside it—he arose and said: “People, slaughter your sacrificial animals and shave your heads.” No one stood.
He repeated the command, but no one stood. He repeated it a third time, yet still no one rose.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the tent of Umm Salamah and asked: “Umm Salamah, what is the matter with the people?”
She replied, “Messenger of Allah, they have been overwhelmed by the grief you have seen. Do not speak to any of them. Go directly to your sacrificial animal, slaughter it and shave your head. Once you have done so, the people will follow.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out without speaking to anyone. He approached his sacrificial animal and slaughtered it, then sat down and had his head shaved. The people immediately arose, slaughtered their animals and shaved their heads.
When they reached the middle of the road between Makkah and Madinah, Sūrat al-Fatḥ was revealed.
Good: Related by Imām Aḥmad (18910) and Ibn Hishām in al-Sīrah (2/308). Some passages in Ibn Isḥāq’s account are open to question, including the statement that the people numbered seven hundred, as explained shortly before.

٩٠١١ — عن المسور بن مخرمة ومروان بن الحكم قالا: خرج رسول الله ﷺ عام الحديبية يريد زيارة البيت، لا يريد قتالًا، وساق معه الهدي سبعين بدنة، وكان الناس سبعمائة رجل، فكانت كل بدنة عن عشرة.
وخرج رسول الله ﷺ حتى إذا كان بعسفان لقيه بشر بن سفيان الكعبي، فقال: يا رسول الله، هذه قريش قد سمعت بمسيرك، فخرجت معها العوذ المطافيل، قد لبسوا جلود النمور، يعاهدون الله ألا تدخلها عليهم عنوة أبدًا، وهذا خالد بن الوليد في خيلهم قد قدموه إلى كراع الغميم.
فقال رسول الله ﷺ: «يَا وَيْحَ قُرَيْشٍ! لَقَدْ أَكَلَتْهُمُ الْحَرْبُ، مَاذَا عَلَيْهِمْ لَوْ خَلَّوْا بَيْنِي وَبَيْنَ سَائِرِ النَّاسِ؟ فَإِنْ أَصَابُونِي كَانَ الَّذِي أَرَادُوا، وَإِنْ أَظْهَرَنِي اللهُ عَلَيْهِمْ دَخَلُوا فِي الْإِسْلَامِ وَهُمْ وَافِرُونَ، وَإِنْ لَمْ يَفْعَلُوا قَاتَلُوا وَبِهِمْ قُوَّةٌ. فَمَاذَا تَظُنُّ قُرَيْشٌ؟ فَوَاللهِ لَا أَزَالُ أُجَاهِدُهُمْ عَلَى الَّذِي بَعَثَنِي اللهُ بِهِ حَتَّى يُظْهِرَنِي اللهُ، أَوْ تَنْفَرِدَ هَذِهِ السَّالِفَةُ».
ثم أمر الناس فسلكوا ذات اليمين بين ظهري الحمض، على طريق تخرجه على ثنية المرار والحديبية من أسفل مكة. قال: فسلك بالجيش تلك الطريق، فلما رأت خيل قريش قترة الجيش، وقد خالفوا عن طريقهم، ركضوا راجعين إلى قريش.
فخرج رسول الله ﷺ حتى إذا سلك ثنية المرار بركت ناقته، فقال الناس: خلأت. فقال رسول الله ﷺ: «مَا خَلَأَتْ، وَمَا هُوَ لَهَا بِخُلُقٍ، وَلَكِنْ حَبَسَهَا حَابِسُ الْفِيلِ عَنْ مَكَّةَ. وَاللهِ لَا تَدْعُونِي قُرَيْشٌ الْيَوْمَ إِلَى خُطَّةٍ يَسْأَلُونَنِي فِيهَا صِلَةَ الرَّحِمِ إِلَّا أَعْطَيْتُهُمْ إِيَّاهَا».
ثم قال للناس: «انْزِلُوا». فقالوا: يا رسول الله، ما بالوادي من ماء ينزل عليه الناس. فأخرج رسول الله ﷺ سهمًا من كنانته، فأعطاه رجلًا من أصحابه، فنزل في قليب من تلك القُلُب، فغرزه فيه، فجاش الماء حتى ضرب الناس عنه بعطن.
فلما اطمأن رسول الله ﷺ إذا بديل بن ورقاء في رجال من خزاعة، فقال لهم كقوله لبشر بن سفيان. فرجعوا إلى قريش فقالوا: يا معشر قريش، إنكم تعجلون على محمد، وإن محمدًا لم يأت لقتال، إنما جاء زائرًا لهذا البيت، معظمًا لحقه. فاتهموهم.
قال محمد بن إسحاق: قال الزهري: وكانت خزاعة عَيْبَةَ نُصْحِ رسول الله ﷺ، مشركها ومسلمها، لا يخفون على رسول الله ﷺ شيئًا كان بمكة.
فقالوا: وإن كان إنما جاء لذلك، فوالله لا يدخلها أبدًا علينا عنوة، ولا تتحدث بذلك العرب.
ثم بعثوا إليه مكرز بن حفص، أحد بني عامر بن لؤي. فلما رآه رسول الله ﷺ قال: «هَذَا رَجُلٌ غَادِرٌ». فلما انتهى إلى رسول الله ﷺ كلّمه رسول الله ﷺ بنحو ما كلم به أصحابه، ثم رجع إلى قريش فأخبرهم بما قال له رسول الله ﷺ.
قال: فبعثوا إليه الحليس بن علقمة الكناني، وهو يومئذ سيد الأحابيش. فلما رآه رسول الله ﷺ قال: «هَذَا مِنْ قَوْمٍ يَتَأَلَّهُونَ، فَابْعَثُوا الْهَدْيَ فِي وَجْهِهِ».
فبعثوا الهدي، فلما رأى الهدي يسيل عليه من عرض الوادي في قلائده، قد أكل أوباره من طول الحبس عن محله، رجع ولم يصل إلى رسول الله ﷺ إعظامًا لما رأى. فقال: يا معشر قريش، قد رأيت ما لا يحل صده: الهدي في قلائده، قد أكل أوباره من طول الحبس عن محله. قالوا: اجلس، إنما أنت أعرابي لا علم لك.
فبعثوا إليه عروة بن مسعود الثقفي، فقال: يا معشر قريش، إني قد رأيت ما يلقى منكم من تبعثون إلى محمد إذا جاءكم من التعنيف وسوء اللفظ، وقد عرفتم أنكم والد وأني ولد، وقد سمعت بالذي نابكم، فجمعت من أطاعني من قومي، ثم جئت حتى آسيتكم بنفسي. قالوا: صدقت، ما أنت عندنا بمتهم.
فخرج حتى أتى رسول الله ﷺ، فجلس بين يديه، فقال: يا محمد، جمعت أوباش الناس، ثم جئت بهم لبيضتك تفضها! إنها قريش قد خرجت معها العوذ المطافيل، قد لبسوا جلود النمور، يعاهدون الله ألا تدخلها عليهم عنوة أبدًا. وأيم الله، لكأني بهؤلاء قد انكشفوا عنك غدًا.
قال: وأبو بكر قاعد خلف رسول الله ﷺ، فقال: امصص بظر اللات! أنحن ننكشف عنه؟ فقال: من هذا يا محمد؟ قال: «هَذَا ابْنُ أَبِي قُحَافَةَ». قال: أما والله لولا يد كانت لك عندي لكافأتك بها، ولكن هذه بها.
ثم تناول لحية رسول الله ﷺ، والمغيرة بن شعبة واقف على رأس رسول الله ﷺ في الحديد، فقرع يده، ثم قال: أمسك يدك عن لحية رسول الله ﷺ قبل، والله، لا تصل إليك.
قال: ويحك! ما أفظك وأغلظك! فتبسم رسول الله ﷺ. فقال عروة: من هذا يا محمد؟ قال: «هَذَا ابْنُ أَخِيكَ الْمُغِيرَةُ بْنُ شُعْبَةَ». قال: أي غُدَرُ، وهل غسلت سوأتك إلا بالأمس؟
قال: فكلمه رسول الله ﷺ بمثل ما كلم به أصحابه، وأخبره أنه لم يأت يريد حربًا.
فقام من عند رسول الله ﷺ، وقد رأى ما يصنع به أصحابه: لا يتوضأ وضوءًا إلا ابتدروه، ولا يبصق بصاقًا إلا ابتدروه، ولا يسقط من شعره شيء إلا أخذوه.
فرجع إلى قريش فقال: يا معشر قريش، إني جئت كسرى في ملكه، وجئت قيصر والنجاشي في ملكهما. والله ما رأيت ملكًا قط مثل محمد في أصحابه، ولقد رأيت قومًا لا يسلمونه لشيء أبدًا، فروا رأيكم.
قال: وكان رسول الله ﷺ قبل ذلك قد بعث خراش بن أمية الخزاعي إلى مكة، وحمله على جمل له، ليبلغ أشرافهم عنه ما جاء له. فعقروا به جمل رسول الله ﷺ، وأرادوا قتله، فمنعته الأحابيش، فخلوا سبيله حتى أتى رسول الله ﷺ.
فدعا عمر ليبعثه إلى مكة، فقال: يا رسول الله، إني أخاف قريشًا على نفسي، وليس بها من بني عدي أحد يمنعني، وقد عرفت قريش عداوتي إياها وغلظتي عليها، ولكن أدلك على رجل هو أعز مني: عثمان بن عفان.
قال: فدعاه رسول الله ﷺ، فبعثه إلى قريش يخبرهم أنه لم يأت لحرب أحد، وإنما جاء زائرًا لهذا البيت، معظمًا لحرمته.
فخرج عثمان حتى أتى مكة، فلقيه أبان بن سعيد بن العاص، فنزل عن دابته وحمله بين يديه، وردف خلفه، وأجاره حتى بلغ رسالة رسول الله ﷺ.
فانطلق عثمان حتى أتى أبا سفيان وعظماء قريش، فبلغهم عن رسول الله ﷺ ما أرسله به. فقالوا لعثمان: إن شئت أن تطوف بالبيت فطف به. فقال: ما كنت لأفعل حتى يطوف به رسول الله ﷺ. قال: واحتبسته قريش عندها، وبلغ رسول الله ﷺ أن عثمان قد قتل.
قال محمد: فحدثني الزهري أن قريشًا بعثوا سهيل بن عمرو، أحد بني عامر بن لؤي، وقالوا: ائت محمدًا فصالحه، ولا يكن في صلحه إلا أن يرجع عنا عامه هذا، فوالله لا تتحدث العرب أنه دخلها علينا عنوة أبدًا.
فأتاه سهيل بن عمرو، فلما رآه النبي ﷺ قال: «قَدْ أَرَادَ الْقَوْمُ الصُّلْحَ حِينَ بَعَثُوا هَذَا الرَّجُلَ».
فلما انتهى إلى رسول الله ﷺ تكلما وأطالا الكلام، وتراجعا حتى جرى بينهما الصلح. فلما التأم الأمر ولم يبق إلا الكتاب، وثب عمر بن الخطاب فأتى أبا بكر، فقال: يا أبا بكر، أوليس برسول الله؟ أولسنا بالمسلمين؟ أوليسوا بالمشركين؟ قال: بلى. قال: فعلام نعطي الذلة في ديننا؟
فقال أبو بكر: يا عمر، الزم غرزه حيث كان، فإني أشهد أنه رسول الله. قال عمر: وأنا أشهد.
ثم أتى رسول الله ﷺ فقال: يا رسول الله، أولسنا بالمسلمين؟ أوليسوا بالمشركين؟ قال: «بَلَى». قال: فعلام نعطي الذلة في ديننا؟
فقال: «أَنَا عَبْدُ اللهِ وَرَسُولُهُ، لَنْ أُخَالِفَ أَمْرَهُ، وَلَنْ يُضَيِّعَنِي».
ثم قال عمر: ما زلت أصوم وأصلي وأتصدق وأعتق من الذي صنعت، مخافة كلامي الذي تكلمت به يومئذ، حتى رجوت أن يكون خيرًا.
قال: ودعا رسول الله ﷺ علي بن أبي طالب فقال: «اكْتُبْ: بِسْمِ اللهِ الرَّحْمَنِ الرَّحِيمِ». فقال سهيل بن عمرو: لا أعرف هذا، ولكن اكتب: باسمك اللهم.
فقال رسول الله ﷺ: «اكْتُبْ: بِاسْمِكَ اللَّهُمَّ. هَذَا مَا صَالَحَ عَلَيْهِ مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اللهِ سُهَيْلَ بْنَ عَمْرٍو».
فقال: لو شهدت أنك رسول الله لم أقاتلك، ولكن اكتب: هذا ما اصطلح عليه محمد بن عبد الله وسهيل بن عمرو.
على وضع الحرب عشر سنين، يأمن فيهن الناس، ويكف بعضهم عن بعض؛ على أنه من أتى رسول الله ﷺ من أصحابه بغير إذن وليه رده عليهم، ومن أتى قريشًا ممن مع رسول الله ﷺ لم يردوه عليه؛ وأن بيننا عَيْبَةً مَكْفُوفَةً؛ وأنه لا إسلال ولا إغلال.
وكان في شرطهم حين كتبوا الكتاب: أنه من أحب أن يدخل في عقد محمد وعهده دخل فيه، ومن أحب أن يدخل في عقد قريش وعهدهم دخل فيه.
فتواثبت خزاعة فقالوا: نحن في عقد رسول الله ﷺ وعهده. وتواثبت بنو بكر فقالوا: نحن في عقد قريش وعهدهم.
وأنك ترجع عنا عامنا هذا فلا تدخل علينا مكة، وأنه إذا كان عام قابل خرجنا عنك، فتدخلها بأصحابك، وأقمت فيهم ثلاثًا، معك سلاح الراكب، لا تدخلها بغير السيوف في القرب.
فبينما رسول الله ﷺ يكتب الكتاب إذا جاءه أبو جندل بن سهيل بن عمرو في الحديد، قد انفلت إلى رسول الله ﷺ.
قال: وقد كان أصحاب رسول الله ﷺ خرجوا وهم لا يشكون في الفتح، لرؤيا رآها رسول الله ﷺ. فلما رأوا ما رأوا من الصلح والرجوع، وما تحمل رسول الله ﷺ على نفسه، دخل الناس من ذلك أمر عظيم، حتى كادوا أن يهلكوا.
فلما رأى سهيل أبا جندل قام إليه فضرب وجهه وقال: يا محمد، قد لجت القضية بيني وبينك قبل أن يأتيك هذا. قال: «صَدَقْتَ». فقام إليه فأخذ بتلابيبه.
قال: وصرخ أبو جندل بأعلى صوته: يا معشر المسلمين، أتردونني إلى أهل الشرك فيفتنوني في ديني؟ قال: فزاد الناس شرًّا إلى ما بهم.
فقال رسول الله ﷺ: «يَا أَبَا جَنْدَلٍ، اصْبِرْ وَاحْتَسِبْ؛ فَإِنَّ اللهَ جَاعِلٌ لَكَ وَلِمَنْ مَعَكَ مِنَ الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ فَرَجًا وَمَخْرَجًا. إِنَّا قَدْ عَقَدْنَا بَيْنَنَا وَبَيْنَ الْقَوْمِ صُلْحًا، فَأَعْطَيْنَاهُمْ عَلَى ذَلِكَ وَأَعْطَوْنَا عَلَيْهِ عَهْدًا، وَإِنَّا لَنْ نَغْدِرَ بِهِمْ».
قال: فوثب إليه عمر بن الخطاب، فجعل يمشي مع أبي جندل إلى جنبه، وهو يقول: اصبر يا أبا جندل، فإنما هم المشركون، وإنما دم أحدهم دم كلب. قال: ويدني قائم السيف منه. قال عمر: رجوت أن يأخذ السيف فيضرب به أباه. قال: فضن الرجل بأبيه.
قال: ونفذت القضية. فلما فرغا من الكتاب، وكان رسول الله ﷺ يصلي في الحرم وهو مضطرب في الحل، قام رسول الله ﷺ فقال: «يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ، انْحَرُوا وَاحْلِقُوا». قال: فما قام أحد.
قال: ثم عاد بمثلها، فما قام رجل، حتى عاد ﷺ بمثلها، فما قام رجل.
فرجع رسول الله ﷺ فدخل على أم سلمة فقال: «يَا أُمَّ سَلَمَةَ، مَا شَأْنُ النَّاسِ؟». قالت: يا رسول الله، قد دخلهم ما رأيت، فلا تكلمن منهم إنسانًا، واعمد إلى هديك حيث كان فانحره واحلق، فلو قد فعلت ذلك فعل الناس ذلك.
فخرج رسول الله ﷺ لا يكلم أحدًا، حتى أتى هديه فنحره، ثم جلس فحلق. قال: فقام الناس ينحرون ويحلقون.
قال: حتى إذا كان بين مكة والمدينة في وسط الطريق نزلت سورة الفتح.
حسن: رواه الإمام أحمد (١٨٩١٠)، وابن هشام في «السيرة» (٣٠٨/٢). لكن في بعض فقرات حديث ابن إسحاق نظر، منها قوله: «وكان الناس سبعمائة»، كما سبق بيانه قريبًا.
9011 — Al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam reported: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out during the year of al-Ḥudaybiyyah intending to visit the Sacred House, not to fight. He brought seventy sacrificial camels, while the people numbered seven hundred, so each camel was offered on behalf of ten men.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached ʿUsfān, Bishr ibn Sufyān al-Kaʿbī met him and said, “Messenger of Allah, Quraysh have heard of your approach. They have come out with nursing she-camels and their young, dressed in leopard skins and pledging before Allah that you will never enter Makkah against their will. Khālid ibn al-Walīd has been sent ahead with their cavalry to Kurāʿ al-Ghamīm.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “How unfortunate Quraysh are! War has consumed them. What harm would it do them to leave me to deal with the rest of the people? If they defeat me, that will be what they desire. But if Allah grants me victory, they may enter Islam with their strength intact. If they choose not to, they may then fight while still possessing strength. What do Quraysh imagine? By Allah, I shall continue striving against them for the cause with which Allah sent me until Allah grants me victory or this neck is severed.”
He then instructed the people to take the route to the right through al-Ḥumḍ, along a road leading to the Pass of al-Marār and al-Ḥudaybiyyah from below Makkah. He led the army along that road. When the Quraysh cavalry saw the dust raised by the army and realised that the Muslims had changed their route, they galloped back to Quraysh.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ continued until his she-camel knelt down at the Pass of al-Marār. The people said, “She has become stubborn.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “She has not become stubborn, nor is stubbornness part of her nature. Rather, she has been restrained from Makkah by the One who restrained the elephant. By Allah, Quraysh will not invite me today to any proposal involving the maintenance of kinship without my accepting it.”
He then told the people: “Dismount.” They said, “Messenger of Allah, there is no water in the valley beside which the people can camp.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ took an arrow from his quiver and gave it to one of his Companions. The man descended into one of the wells and planted the arrow in it, whereupon the water surged forth until the people and their animals gathered abundantly around it.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had settled at the campsite, Budayl ibn Warqāʾ arrived with some men of Khuzāʿah. The Prophet ﷺ told them essentially what he had told Bishr ibn Sufyān. They returned to Quraysh and said, “People of Quraysh, you are acting hastily against Muḥammad. Muḥammad has not come to fight; he has come only to visit this House and honour its sanctity.” Quraysh distrusted them.
Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq reported that al-Zuhrī said: Khuzāʿah—both its polytheists and Muslims—were trusted confidants and sincere advisers of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They concealed from him nothing that occurred in Makkah.
Quraysh said, “Even if that is his sole purpose, by Allah, he will never enter Makkah against our will, lest the Arabs speak of it.”
They sent Mikraz ibn Ḥafṣ, a man of Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy, to him. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw him, he said: “This is a treacherous man.” When Mikraz reached him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave him essentially the same message he had given the previous envoys. Mikraz returned to Quraysh and conveyed the Prophet’s words.
They then sent al-Ḥulays ibn ʿAlqamah al-Kinānī, who was the leader of the allied tribes at that time. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw him, he said: “This man belongs to a people who are deeply devoted to religious observances. Send the sacrificial animals out before him.”
The animals were sent toward him, flowing across the breadth of the valley with their garlands upon them. Their hair had become worn from being detained so long from the place of sacrifice. Out of reverence for what he saw, al-Ḥulays turned back without reaching the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He told Quraysh, “I have seen something that it is not lawful to prevent: sacrificial animals wearing their garlands, their hair worn away from being detained so long from their place of sacrifice.” They replied, “Sit down. You are merely a Bedouin with no knowledge.”
They then sent ʿUrwah ibn Masʿūd al-Thaqafī. He said, “People of Quraysh, I have seen how harshly and abusively you treat the men whom you send to Muḥammad when they return. You know that you are like parents to me and I am like a son to you. When I heard of the difficulty that had befallen you, I gathered those of my people who obeyed me and came to support you personally.”
They replied, “You have spoken truthfully. We do not mistrust you.”
He went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, sat before him and said, “Muḥammad, you have gathered the rabble and brought them against your own family to destroy it! Quraysh have come out with nursing she-camels and their young, dressed in leopard skins and pledging before Allah that you will never enter Makkah against their will. By Allah, I can almost see these people abandoning you tomorrow.”
Abū Bakr was sitting behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said, “Go suck al-Lāt’s clitoris! Would we abandon him?”
ʿUrwah asked, “Who is this, Muḥammad?”
He replied: “This is the son of Abū Quḥāfah.”
ʿUrwah said, “By Allah, were it not for a favour you once did me, I would repay your words in kind. Let that favour settle this.”
ʿUrwah then reached for the beard of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah was standing over the Prophet ﷺ in armour, and he struck ʿUrwah’s hand, saying, “Remove your hand from the beard of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ before, by Allah, it is prevented from returning to you.”
ʿUrwah said, “Woe to you! How harsh and coarse you are!” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ smiled.
ʿUrwah asked, “Who is this, Muḥammad?”
He replied: “This is your nephew, al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah.”
ʿUrwah said, “You treacherous man! Was it not only yesterday that I settled the disgrace of your treachery?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave him the same message he had given the previous envoys and informed him that he had not come seeking war.
ʿUrwah then departed, having observed how the Prophet’s Companions treated him: whenever he performed ablution they rushed for the remaining water; whenever he spat they rushed to receive it; and whenever a hair fell from him they picked it up.
He returned to Quraysh and said, “People of Quraysh, I have visited Chosroes in his kingdom, and I have visited Caesar and the Negus in their kingdoms. By Allah, I have never seen any king among his subjects like Muḥammad among his Companions. I have seen people who will never surrender him for anything. Consider carefully what you will do.”
Before that, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had sent Khirāsh ibn Umayyah al-Khuzāʿī to Makkah, mounted upon one of his camels, to inform its chiefs of the purpose for which he had come. Quraysh hamstrung the Messenger’s camel and intended to kill Khirāsh, but the allied tribes protected him. They released him, and he returned to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Prophet ﷺ then summoned ʿUmar to send him to Makkah. ʿUmar said, “Messenger of Allah, I fear that Quraysh may kill me. There is no one from Banū ʿAdī in Makkah to protect me, and Quraysh know my hostility and severity toward them. But I can direct you to a man who possesses greater protection there than I do: ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned ʿUthmān and sent him to Quraysh to inform them that he had not come to fight anyone, but only to visit the Sacred House and honour its sanctity.
ʿUthmān travelled to Makkah, where Abān ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ met him. Abān dismounted, seated ʿUthmān before him on his mount and rode behind him, granting him protection until he could deliver the Messenger’s message.
ʿUthmān went to Abū Sufyān and the leading men of Quraysh and conveyed the message of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. They told him, “If you wish to circumambulate the House, you may do so.”
He replied, “I would never do so before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ circumambulates it.” Quraysh detained him, and word reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that ʿUthmān had been killed.
Muḥammad reported that al-Zuhrī told him: Quraysh sent Suhayl ibn ʿAmr, of Banū ʿĀmir ibn Luʾayy, saying, “Go to Muḥammad and conclude a treaty with him, but the treaty must require him to turn back this year. By Allah, the Arabs must never be allowed to say that he entered Makkah against our will.”
When Suhayl ibn ʿAmr came, the Prophet ﷺ said: “The people now desire peace, since they have sent this man.”
When Suhayl reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, they spoke at length and exchanged proposals until they agreed upon peace. When the matter had been settled and only the written document remained, ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb went to Abū Bakr and asked, “Abū Bakr, is he not the Messenger of Allah? Are we not Muslims? Are they not polytheists?”
He replied, “Indeed.”
ʿUmar asked, “Why, then, should we accept humiliation in our religion?”
Abū Bakr said, “ʿUmar, hold firmly to his stirrup wherever he leads, for I testify that he is the Messenger of Allah.”
ʿUmar replied, “And I testify to that.”
ʿUmar then went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked, “Messenger of Allah, are we not Muslims? Are they not polytheists?”
He replied: “Indeed.”
ʿUmar asked, “Why, then, should we accept humiliation in our religion?”
He replied: “I am Allah’s servant and Messenger. I shall never oppose His command, and He will never abandon me.”
ʿUmar later said: “Because of what I had done and the words I had spoken that day, I continued fasting, praying, giving charity and emancipating slaves until I hoped that the matter had been turned to good.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ summoned ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib and said: “Write: ‘In the name of Allah, the Most Compassionate, the Most Merciful.’”
Suhayl ibn ʿAmr said, “I do not acknowledge this. Write instead: ‘In Your name, O Allah.’”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Write: ‘In Your name, O Allah. This is the treaty concluded by Muḥammad, the Messenger of Allah, with Suhayl ibn ʿAmr.’”
Suhayl said, “Had I acknowledged that you were the Messenger of Allah, I would not have fought you. Write instead: ‘This is the agreement concluded by Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd Allāh and Suhayl ibn ʿAmr.’”
They agreed to suspend warfare for ten years, during which the people would enjoy security and refrain from attacking one another. Any man of Quraysh who came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ without his guardian’s permission would be returned, whereas anyone who left the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for Quraysh would not be returned. Relations between them would be sincere and free of hidden hostility, with neither theft nor treachery.
The written conditions also stipulated that any tribe wishing to enter the alliance and covenant of Muḥammad could do so, and any tribe wishing to enter the alliance and covenant of Quraysh could do so.
Khuzāʿah immediately declared, “We enter the alliance and covenant of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.” Banū Bakr declared, “We enter the alliance and covenant of Quraysh.”
The treaty further stipulated: “You will turn back this year and not enter Makkah. Next year we will withdraw from the city, and you may enter it with your Companions and remain for three days. You may carry only a traveller’s weapons—swords kept in their scabbards.”
While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was having the agreement written, Abū Jandal ibn Suhayl ibn ʿAmr arrived in chains, having escaped to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
The Companions had set out with no doubt that victory would occur because of a vision the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had seen. When they witnessed the treaty, the return without entering Makkah and the concessions the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had accepted, they were overwhelmed by such distress that they nearly perished from grief.
When Suhayl saw Abū Jandal, he went to him, struck him in the face and said, “Muḥammad, our agreement was concluded before this man came to you.”
The Prophet ﷺ said: “You have spoken truthfully.”
Suhayl seized Abū Jandal by the front of his clothing. Abū Jandal cried out at the top of his voice, “Muslims! Will you return me to the polytheists so that they may persecute me for my religion?” This only intensified the people’s anguish.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Abū Jandal, remain patient and seek your reward from Allah. Allah will provide relief and a way out for you and the other oppressed Muslims with you. We have concluded a treaty with these people, giving them our covenant and receiving theirs in return. We will not betray them.”
ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb went to Abū Jandal and walked beside him, saying, “Be patient, Abū Jandal. They are only polytheists, and the blood of any one of them is merely the blood of a dog.” ʿUmar brought the sword’s hilt close to him, hoping that he would seize it and strike his father, but Abū Jandal could not bring himself to kill his father.
The agreement was carried into effect. When they had finished writing it—the Messenger of Allah ﷺ praying within the sacred precinct while his camp stood outside it—he arose and said: “People, slaughter your sacrificial animals and shave your heads.” No one stood.
He repeated the command, but no one stood. He repeated it a third time, yet still no one rose.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the tent of Umm Salamah and asked: “Umm Salamah, what is the matter with the people?”
She replied, “Messenger of Allah, they have been overwhelmed by the grief you have seen. Do not speak to any of them. Go directly to your sacrificial animal, slaughter it and shave your head. Once you have done so, the people will follow.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out without speaking to anyone. He approached his sacrificial animal and slaughtered it, then sat down and had his head shaved. The people immediately arose, slaughtered their animals and shaved their heads.
When they reached the middle of the road between Makkah and Madinah, Sūrat al-Fatḥ was revealed.
Good: Related by Imām Aḥmad (18910) and Ibn Hishām in al-Sīrah (2/308). Some passages in Ibn Isḥāq’s account are open to question, including the statement that the people numbered seven hundred, as explained shortly before.

٩٠١٢ — عن المغيرة بن شعبة أنه كان قائمًا على رأس رسول الله ﷺ بالسيف، وهو ملثم، وعنده عروة. قال: فجعل عروة يتناول لحية النبي ﷺ ويحدثه. قال: فقال المغيرة لعروة: لتكفن يدك عن لحيته، أو لا ترجع إليك.
قال: فقال عروة: من هذا؟ قال: هذا ابن أخيك المغيرة بن شعبة. فقال عروة: يا غُدَرُ، ما غسلت رأسك من غدرتك بعد.
صحيح: رواه أبو بكر بن أبي شيبة كما في «المطالب» (٢١١٦)، وصححه ابن حبان (٤٥٨٣)، واللفظ لابن حبان.

english_source:
9012 — Al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah reported that he stood over the Messenger of Allah ﷺ carrying a sword, with his face covered, while ʿUrwah was present. As ʿUrwah spoke to the Prophet ﷺ, he repeatedly reached for his beard.
Al-Mughīrah said to him, “Keep your hand away from his beard, or it will not return to you.”
ʿUrwah asked, “Who is this?”
He was told, “This is your nephew, al-Mughīrah ibn Shuʿbah.”
ʿUrwah said, “You treacherous man! You have not yet cleansed your head of your treachery.”
Authentic: Related by Abū Bakr ibn Abī Shaybah, as cited in al-Maṭālib (2116), and authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (4583). The wording is that of Ibn Ḥibbān.

٩٠١٣ — عن سلمة بن الأكوع قال: قدمنا الحديبية مع رسول الله ﷺ ونحن أربع عشرة مائة، وعليها خمسون شاة لا ترويها. قال: فقعد رسول الله ﷺ على جَبَا الرَّكِيَّة، فإما دعا وإما بصق فيها. قال: فجاشت، فسقينا واستقينا.
قال: ثم إن رسول الله ﷺ دعانا للبيعة في أصل الشجرة. قال: فبايعته أول الناس، ثم بايع وبايع، حتى إذا كان في وسط من الناس قال: «بَايِعْ يَا سَلَمَةُ!». قال: قلت: قد بايعتك يا رسول الله في أول الناس. قال: «وَأَيْضًا».
قال: ورآني رسول الله ﷺ عَزِلًا، يعني ليس معه سلاح، فأعطاني رسول الله ﷺ حجفة أو درقة. ثم بايع حتى إذا كان في آخر الناس قال: «أَلَا تُبَايِعُنِي يَا سَلَمَةُ؟». قلت: قد بايعتك يا رسول الله في أول الناس وفي أوسط الناس. قال: «وَأَيْضًا». فبايعته الثالثة.
ثم قال لي: «يَا سَلَمَةُ، أَيْنَ حَجَفَتُكَ أَوْ دَرَقَتُكَ الَّتِي أَعْطَيْتُكَ؟». قلت: يا رسول الله، لقيني عمي عامر عزلًا فأعطيته إياها. فضحك رسول الله ﷺ وقال: «إِنَّكَ كَالَّذِي قَالَ الْأَوَّلُ: اللَّهُمَّ أَبْغِنِي حَبِيبًا هُوَ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِنْ نَفْسِي».
ثم إن المشركين راسلونا الصلح، حتى مشى بعضنا في بعض واصطلحنا. قال: وكنت تَبِيعًا لطلحة بن عبيد الله، أسقي فرسه وأحسه وأخدمه، وآكل من طعامه. وتركت أهلي ومالي مهاجرًا إلى الله ورسوله ﷺ.
قال: فلما اصطلحنا نحن وأهل مكة، واختلط بعضنا ببعض، أتيت شجرة فكسحت شوكها، فاضطجعت في أصلها. فأتاني أربعة من المشركين من أهل مكة، فجعلوا يقعون في رسول الله ﷺ، فأبغضتهم.
فتحوّلت إلى شجرة أخرى، وعلقوا سلاحهم واضطجعوا. فبينما هم كذلك إذ نادى مناد من أسفل الوادي: يا للمهاجرين! قُتل ابن زنيم!
قال: فاخترطت سيفي، ثم شددت على أولئك الأربعة وهم رقود، فأخذت سلاحهم فجعلته ضِغثًا في يدي، ثم قلت: والذي كرّم وجه محمد، لا يرفع أحد منكم رأسه إلا ضربت الذي فيه عيناه.
ثم جئت بهم أسوقهم إلى رسول الله ﷺ. وجاء عمي عامر برجل من العَبَلات يقال له مكرز، يقوده إلى رسول الله ﷺ على فرس مجفف، في سبعين من المشركين.
فنظر إليهم رسول الله ﷺ فقال: «دَعُوهُمْ، يَكُنْ لَهُمْ بَدْءُ الْفُجُورِ وَثِنَاهُ». فعفا عنهم رسول الله ﷺ، وأنزل الله: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي كَفَّ أَيْدِيَهُمْ عَنْكُمْ وَأَيْدِيَكُمْ عَنْهُمْ بِبَطْنِ مَكَّةَ مِنْ بَعْدِ أَنْ أَظْفَرَكُمْ عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ [الفتح: ٢٤]، الآية كلها.
قال: ثم خرجنا راجعين إلى المدينة، فنزلنا منزلًا بيننا وبين بني لحيان جبل، وهم المشركون. فاستغفر رسول الله ﷺ لمن رقي هذا الجبل الليلة، أنه طليعة للنبي ﷺ وأصحابه. قال سلمة: فرقيت تلك الليلة مرتين أو ثلاثًا.
ثم قدمنا المدينة، فبعث رسول الله ﷺ بظهره مع رباح، غلام رسول الله ﷺ، وأنا معه. وخرجت معه بفرس طلحة أندّيه مع الظهر.
فلما أصبحنا إذا عبد الرحمن الفزاري قد أغار على ظهر رسول الله ﷺ، فاستاقه أجمع وقتل راعيه.
فقلت: يا رباح، خذ هذا الفرس فأبلغه طلحة بن عبيد الله، وأخبر رسول الله ﷺ أن المشركين قد أغاروا على سرحه.
ثم قمت على أكمة فاستقبلت المدينة، فناديت ثلاثًا: يا صباحاه! ثم خرجت في آثار القوم أرميهم بالنبل وأرتجز، أقول:
أنا ابن الأكوع
 واليوم يوم الرُّضَّع
فألحق رجلًا منهم، فأصك سهمًا في رحله، حتى خلص نصل السهم إلى كتفه. قلت:
خذها وأنا ابن الأكوع
 واليوم يوم الرضع
فوالله ما زلت أرميهم وأعقر بهم. فإذا رجع إليَّ فارس أتيت شجرة فجلست في أصلها، ثم رميته فعقرت به. حتى إذا تضايق الجبل فدخلوا في مضايقه، علوت الجبل فجعلت أرديهم بالحجارة.
فما زلت كذلك أتبعهم حتى ما خلق الله من بعير من ظهر رسول الله ﷺ إلا خلفته وراء ظهري، وخلوا بيني وبينه.
ثم أتبعتهم أرميهم حتى ألقوا أكثر من ثلاثين بردة وثلاثين رمحًا يستخفون، ولا يطرحون شيئًا إلا جعلت عليه آرامًا من الحجارة، يعرفها رسول الله ﷺ وأصحابه.
حتى إذا أتوا مضيقًا من ثنية، فإذا هم قد أتاهم فلان بن بدر الفزاري، فجلسوا يتضحّون، يعني يتغدون. وجلست على رأس قرن.
قال الفزاري: ما هذا الذي أرى؟ قالوا: لقينا من هذا البَرْحَ! والله ما فارقنا منذ غلس، يرمينا حتى انتزع كل شيء في أيدينا.
قال: فليقم إليه نفر منكم، أربعة. قال: فصعد إلي منهم أربعة في الجبل. فلما أمكنوني من الكلام قلت: هل تعرفونني؟ قالوا: لا، ومن أنت؟ قلت: أنا سلمة بن الأكوع. والذي كرّم وجه محمد، لا أطلب رجلًا منكم إلا أدركته، ولا يطلبني رجل منكم فيدركني.
قال أحدهم: أنا أظن. قال: فرجعوا.
فما برحت مكاني حتى رأيت فوارس رسول الله ﷺ يتخللون الشجر. فإذا أولهم الأخرم الأسدي، وعلى أثره أبو قتادة الأنصاري، وعلى أثره المقداد بن الأسود الكندي.
فأخذت بعنان الأخرم، فولوا مدبرين. قلت: يا أخرم، احذرهم، لا يقتطعوك حتى يلحق رسول الله ﷺ وأصحابه.
قال: يا سلمة، إن كنت تؤمن بالله واليوم الآخر، وتعلم أن الجنة حق والنار حق، فلا تحل بيني وبين الشهادة. قال: فخليته.
فالتقى هو وعبد الرحمن، فعقر بعبد الرحمن فرسه، وطعنه عبد الرحمن فقتله، وتحول على فرسه. ولحق أبو قتادة، فارس رسول الله ﷺ، بعبد الرحمن فطعنه فقتله.
فوالذي كرّم وجه محمد، اتبعتهم أعدو على رجلي حتى ما أرى ورائي من أصحاب محمد ﷺ ولا غبارهم شيئًا، حتى عدلوا قبل غروب الشمس إلى شعب فيه ماء يقال له: ذو قرد، ليشربوا منه وهم عطاش.
فنظروا إلي أعدو وراءهم، فحلأتهم عنه، فما ذاقوا منه قطرة. وخرجوا يشتدون في ثنية.
فأعدو فألحق رجلًا منهم، فأصكه بسهم في نغض كتفه، فقلت:
خذها وأنا ابن الأكوع
 واليوم يوم الرضع
قال: يا ثكلته أمه! أكوعه بكرة؟ قلت: نعم، يا عدو نفسه، أكوعك بكرة.
قال: وأردوا فرسين على ثنية، فجئت بهما أسوقهما إلى رسول الله ﷺ.
ولحقني عامر بسطيحة فيها مذقة من لبن، وسطيحة فيها ماء، فتوضأت وشربت، ثم أتيت رسول الله ﷺ وهو على الماء الذي حلأتهم عنه.
فإذا رسول الله ﷺ قد أخذ تلك الإبل، وكل شيء استنقذته من المشركين، وكل رمح وبردة. وإذا بلال قد نحر ناقة من الإبل التي استنقذت من القوم، وإذا هو يشوي لرسول الله ﷺ من كبدها وسنامها.
قلت: يا رسول الله، خلني فأنتخب من القوم مائة رجل، فأتبع القوم فلا يبقى منهم مخبر إلا قتلته.
فضحك رسول الله ﷺ حتى بدت نواجذه في ضوء النار، فقال: «يَا سَلَمَةُ، أَتُرَاكَ كُنْتَ فَاعِلًا؟». قلت: نعم، والذي أكرمك!
فقال: «إِنَّهُمُ الْآنَ لَيُقْرَوْنَ فِي أَرْضِ غَطَفَانَ».
قال: فجاء رجل من غطفان فقال: نحر لهم فلان جزورًا، فلما كشفوا جلدها رأوا غبارًا، فقالوا: أتاكم القوم، فخرجوا هاربين.
فلما أصبحنا قال رسول الله ﷺ: «كَانَ خَيْرُ فُرْسَانِنَا الْيَوْمَ أَبُو قَتَادَةَ، وَخَيْرُ رَجَّالَتِنَا سَلَمَةُ».
ثم أعطاني رسول الله ﷺ سهمين: سهم الفارس وسهم الراجل، فجمعهما لي جميعًا. ثم أردفني رسول الله ﷺ وراءه على العضباء، راجعين إلى المدينة.
قال: فبينما نحن نسير، وكان رجل من الأنصار لا يُسبق شدًّا، فجعل يقول: ألا مسابق إلى المدينة؟ هل من مسابق؟ فجعل يعيد ذلك.
فلما سمعت كلامه قلت: أما تكرم كريمًا ولا تهاب شريفًا؟ قال: لا، إلا أن يكون رسول الله ﷺ.
قلت: يا رسول الله، بأبي أنت وأمي، ذرني فلأسابق الرجل. قال: «إِنْ شِئْتَ».
قلت: اذهب إليك. وثنيت رجلي فطفرت فعدوت. فربطت عليه شرفًا أو شرفين أستبقي نفسي، ثم عدوت في إثره. فربطت عليه شرفًا أو شرفين، ثم إني رفعت حتى ألحقه، فأصكه بين كتفيه، فقلت: قد سبقت، والله! قال: أنا أظن. فسبقته إلى المدينة.
فوالله ما لبثنا إلا ثلاث ليال حتى خرجنا إلى خيبر مع رسول الله ﷺ. فجعل عمي عامر يرتجز بالقوم:
تالله لولا الله ما اهتدينا
 ولا تصدقنا ولا صلينا
 ونحن عن فضلك ما استغنينا
 فثبت الأقدام إن لاقينا
 وأنزلن سكينة علينا
فقال رسول الله ﷺ: «مَنْ هَذَا؟». قال: أنا عامر. قال: «غَفَرَ لَكَ رَبُّكَ».
قال: وما استغفر رسول الله ﷺ لإنسان يخصه إلا استشهد. فنادى عمر بن الخطاب، وهو على جمل له: يا نبي الله، لولا ما متعتنا بعامر!
فلما قدمنا خيبر خرج ملكهم مرحب يخطر بسيفه ويقول:
قد علمت خيبر أني مرحب
 شاكي السلاح بطل مجرب
 إذا الحروب أقبلت تلهب
وبرز له عمي عامر فقال:
قد علمت خيبر أني عامر
 شاكي السلاح بطل مغامر
فاختلفا ضربتين، فوقع سيف مرحب في ترس عامر، وذهب عامر يسفل له، فرجع سيفه على نفسه فقطع أكحله، فكانت فيها نفسه.
قال سلمة: فخرجت فإذا نفر من أصحاب النبي ﷺ يقولون: بطل عمل عامر، قتل نفسه. فأتيت النبي ﷺ وأنا أبكي، فقلت: يا رسول الله، بطل عمل عامر؟
فقال رسول الله ﷺ: «مَنْ قَالَ ذَلِكَ؟». قلت: ناس من أصحابك. قال: «كَذَبَ مَنْ قَالَ ذَلِكَ، بَلْ لَهُ أَجْرُهُ مَرَّتَيْنِ».
ثم أرسلني إلى علي، وهو أرمد، فقال: «لَأُعْطِيَنَّ الرَّايَةَ رَجُلًا يُحِبُّ اللهَ وَرَسُولَهُ، أَوْ يُحِبُّهُ اللهُ وَرَسُولُهُ».
قال: فأتيت عليًّا، فجئت به أقوده وهو أرمد، حتى أتيت به رسول الله ﷺ، فبصق في عينيه فبرأ، وأعطاه الراية.
وخرج مرحب فقال:
قد علمت خيبر أني مرحب
 شاكي السلاح بطل مجرب
 إذا الحروب أقبلت تلهب
فقال علي:
أنا الذي سمتني أمي حيدره
 كليث غابات كريه المنظره
 أوفيهم بالصاع كيل السندره
قال: فضرب رأس مرحب فقتله، ثم كان الفتح على يديه.
