٩٠٢٣ — عن أبي وائل قال: قام سهل بن حنيف يوم صفين فقال: أيها الناس، اتهموا أنفسكم. لقد كنا مع رسول الله ﷺ يوم الحديبية، ولو نرى قتالًا لقاتلنا، وذلك في الصلح الذي كان بين رسول الله ﷺ وبين المشركين.
فجاء عمر بن الخطاب، فأتى رسول الله ﷺ فقال: يا رسول الله، ألسنا على حق وهم على باطل؟ قال: «بَلَى». قال: أليس قتلانا في الجنة وقتلاهم في النار؟ قال: «بَلَى». قال: ففيم نعطي الدنية في ديننا، ونرجع ولما يحكم الله بيننا وبينهم؟
فقال: «يَا ابْنَ الْخَطَّابِ، إِنِّي رَسُولُ اللهِ، وَلَنْ يُضَيِّعَنِي اللهُ أَبَدًا».
قال: فانطلق عمر، فلم يصبر متغيظًا، فأتى أبا بكر فقال: يا أبا بكر، ألسنا على حق وهم على باطل؟ قال: بلى. قال: أليس قتلانا في الجنة وقتلاهم في النار؟ قال: بلى. قال: فعلام نعطي الدنية في ديننا، ونرجع ولما يحكم الله بيننا وبينهم؟
فقال: يا ابن الخطاب، إنه رسول الله، ولن يضيعه الله أبدًا.
قال: فنزل القرآن على رسول الله ﷺ بالفتح، فأرسل إلى عمر فأقرأه إياه. فقال: يا رسول الله، أوَفتح هو؟ قال: «نَعَمْ». فطابت نفسه ورجع.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٣١٨٢)، ومسلم (٩٤:١٧٨٥).

9023 — Abū Wāʾil reported: On the day of Ṣiffīn, Sahl ibn Ḥunayf stood and said:
“People, distrust your own opinions. We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the day of al-Ḥudaybiyyah, and had we considered fighting appropriate, we would have fought. This occurred during the treaty between the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the polytheists.
“ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and asked, ‘Messenger of Allah, are we not upon the truth and they upon falsehood?’
“He replied: ‘Indeed.’
“ʿUmar asked, ‘Are not our dead in Paradise and their dead in the Fire?’
“He replied: ‘Indeed.’
“ʿUmar asked, ‘Why, then, should we accept humiliation in our religion and turn back before Allah has judged between us and them?’
“He replied: ‘Son of al-Khaṭṭāb, I am the Messenger of Allah, and Allah will never abandon me.’”
Still deeply agitated, ʿUmar went to Abū Bakr and asked, “Abū Bakr, are we not upon the truth and they upon falsehood?”
He replied, “Indeed.”
ʿUmar asked, “Are not our dead in Paradise and their dead in the Fire?”
He replied, “Indeed.”
ʿUmar asked, “Why, then, should we accept humiliation in our religion and turn back before Allah has judged between us and them?”
Abū Bakr replied, “Son of al-Khaṭṭāb, he is the Messenger of Allah, and Allah will never abandon him.”
The revelation announcing the victory then descended upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He sent for ʿUmar and recited it to him.
ʿUmar asked, “Messenger of Allah, is this truly a victory?”
He replied: “Yes.”
ʿUmar’s heart then became content and he withdrew his objection.
Agreed upon: Related by al-Bukhārī (3182) and Muslim (1785:94).

arabic_source:
٩٠٢٤ — عن أنس بن مالك في قوله تعالى: ﴿إِنَّا فَتَحْنَا لَكَ فَتْحًا مُبِينًا﴾ [الفتح: ١] قال: الحديبية. قال أصحابه: هنيئًا مريئًا، فما لنا؟ فأنزل الله: ﴿لِيُدْخِلَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُؤْمِنَاتِ جَنَّاتٍ﴾ [الفتح: ٥].
قال شعبة: فقدمت الكوفة فحدثت بهذا كله عن قتادة، ثم رجعت فذكرته له، فقال: أما ﴿إِنَّا فَتَحْنَا لَكَ﴾ فعن أنس، وأما «هنيئًا مريئًا» فعن عكرمة.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤١٧٢)، ومسلم (٩٧:١٧٨٦).
ومن وجه آخر عند مسلم أن أنس بن مالك حدثهم قال: لما نزلت: ﴿إِنَّا فَتَحْنَا لَكَ﴾ إلى قوله: ﴿فَوْزًا عَظِيمًا﴾ [الفتح: ١-٥]، مرجعه من الحديبية، وهم يخالطون الحزن والكآبة، وقد نحر الهدي بالحديبية، فقال: «لَقَدْ أُنْزِلَتْ عَلَيَّ آيَةٌ هِيَ أَحَبُّ إِلَيَّ مِنَ الدُّنْيَا جَمِيعًا».
وكان صلح الحديبية سببًا لفتح مكة؛ لأن هذا الصلح لم يستمر أكثر من سبعة عشر أو ثمانية عشر شهرًا، حيث أعانت قريش حلفاءها بني بكر ضد خزاعة حلفاء المسلمين، كما سيأتي في فتح مكة. انظر: «البداية والنهاية» (٥٠٨/٦).

9024 — Anas ibn Mālik explained the verse, “Indeed, We have granted you a manifest victory” [al-Fatḥ 48:1], saying: “It refers to al-Ḥudaybiyyah.”
The Companions said, “May it bring you happiness and blessing, but what has been granted to us?” Allah then revealed: “So that He may admit believing men and believing women into gardens…” [al-Fatḥ 48:5].
Shuʿbah said: I went to Kūfah and related this entire account from Qatādah. When I later returned and mentioned it to him, he said: “The explanation of ‘Indeed, We have granted you a manifest victory’ is from Anas, while the words ‘May it bring you happiness and blessing’ are from ʿIkrimah.”
Agreed upon: Related by al-Bukhārī (4172) and Muslim (1786:97).
In another route related by Muslim, Anas ibn Mālik said: When the verses beginning, “Indeed, We have granted you a manifest victory,” through the words, “a supreme triumph” [al-Fatḥ 48:1–5], were revealed during the Prophet’s return from al-Ḥudaybiyyah, the Companions were overcome with sorrow and dejection, and the sacrificial animals had already been slaughtered there. The Prophet ﷺ said: “A verse has been revealed to me that is dearer to me than the entire world.”
The Treaty of al-Ḥudaybiyyah became a cause of the conquest of Makkah. It lasted no more than seventeen or eighteen months before Quraysh assisted its allies, Banū Bakr, against Khuzāʿah, the allies of the Muslims, as will be related in the account of the conquest of Makkah. See al-Bidāyah wa-al-Nihāyah (6/508).

٩٠٢٥ — عن سلمة بن الأكوع قال: خرجت قبل أن يؤذن بالأولى، وكانت لقاح رسول الله ﷺ ترعى بذي قرد. فلقيني غلام لعبد الرحمن بن عوف فقال: أُخذت لقاح رسول الله ﷺ. قلت: من أخذها؟ قال: غطفان.
فصرخت ثلاث صرخات: يا صباحاه! فأسمعت ما بين لابتي المدينة، ثم اندفعت على وجهي حتى أدركتهم وقد أخذوا يستقون من الماء.
فجعلت أرميهم بنبلي، وكنت راميًا، وأقول:
أنا ابن الأكوع
 اليوم يوم الرضع
فارتجز حتى استنقذت اللقاح منهم، واستلبت منهم ثلاثين بردة.
وجاء النبي ﷺ والناس، فقلت: يا نبي الله، إني قد حميت القوم الماء وهم عطاش، فابعث إليهم الساعة.
فقال: «يَا ابْنَ الْأَكْوَعِ، مَلَكْتَ فَأَسْجِحْ».
ثم رجعنا، ويردفني رسول الله ﷺ على ناقته حتى دخلنا المدينة.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري في المغازي (٤١٩٤) ومسلم في الجهاد (١٣١:١٨٠٦)، كلاهما عن قتيبة بن سعيد، حدثنا حاتم بن إسماعيل، عن يزيد بن أبي عبيد قال: سمعت سلمة بن الأكوع يقول: فذكره.
قوله: «لقاح» واحدة لقحة، وهي ذات اللبن القريبة العهد بالولادة.

english_source:
9025 — Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ reported: I went out before the call to the dawn prayer. The milch camels of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were grazing at Dhū Qarad. A servant of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf met me and said, “The milch camels of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ have been taken.”
I asked, “Who took them?”
He replied, “Ghaṭafān.”
I cried three times, “Alarm! Alarm!” making myself heard throughout the area between the two lava fields of Madinah. I then rushed forward until I caught them as they were drawing water.
I began shooting arrows at them, for I was a skilled archer, while chanting:
I am the son of al-Akwaʿ;
 today is the day the cowardly will perish.
I continued chanting and fighting until I recovered the camels and seized thirty cloaks from them.
The Prophet ﷺ and the people arrived. I said, “Prophet of Allah, I have kept them away from the water while they are thirsty. Send a force against them immediately.”
He replied: “Son of al-Akwaʿ, now that you have prevailed, show leniency.”
We then returned, with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seating me behind him upon his she-camel until we entered Madinah.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī in al-Maghāzī (4194) and Muslim in al-Jihād (1806:131), both from Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥātim ibn Ismāʿīl, from Yazīd ibn Abī ʿUbayd, who heard Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ.
The singular of liqāḥ is laqḥah: a milk-producing she-camel that has recently given birth.

قوله: «لقاح» واحدة لقحة، وهي ذات اللبن القريبة العهد بالولادة.
9025 — Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ reported: I went out before the call to the dawn prayer. The milch camels of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ were grazing at Dhū Qarad. A servant of ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf met me and said, “The milch camels of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ have been taken.”
I asked, “Who took them?”
He replied, “Ghaṭafān.”
I cried three times, “Alarm! Alarm!” making myself heard throughout the area between the two lava fields of Madinah. I then rushed forward until I caught them as they were drawing water.
I began shooting arrows at them, for I was a skilled archer, while chanting:
I am the son of al-Akwaʿ;
 today is the day the cowardly will perish.
I continued chanting and fighting until I recovered the camels and seized thirty cloaks from them.
The Prophet ﷺ and the people arrived. I said, “Prophet of Allah, I have kept them away from the water while they are thirsty. Send a force against them immediately.”
He replied: “Son of al-Akwaʿ, now that you have prevailed, show leniency.”
We then returned, with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ seating me behind him upon his she-camel until we entered Madinah.
Agreed upon: Narrated by al-Bukhārī in al-Maghāzī (4194) and Muslim in al-Jihād (1806:131), both from Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥātim ibn Ismāʿīl, from Yazīd ibn Abī ʿUbayd, who heard Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ.
The singular of liqāḥ is laqḥah: a milk-producing she-camel that has recently given birth.

٩٠٢٦ — عن مروان بن الحكم والمسور بن مخرمة قالا: انصرف رسول الله ﷺ عام الحديبية، فنزلت عليه سورة الفتح فيما بين مكة والمدينة، فأعطاه الله عز وجل فيها خيبر: ﴿وَعَدَكُمُ اللهُ مَغَانِمَ كَثِيرَةً تَأْخُذُونَهَا فَعَجَّلَ لَكُمْ هَذِهِ﴾ [الفتح: ٢٠].
فقدم رسول الله ﷺ في ذي الحجة، فأقام بها حتى سار إلى خيبر في المحرم. فنزل رسول الله ﷺ بالرجيع، وادٍ بين خيبر وغطفان، فتخوف أن تمدهم غطفان، فبات بها حتى أصبح، فغدا إليهم.
حسن: رواه محمد بن إسحاق، قال: حدثني الزهري، عن عروة، عن مروان بن الحكم والمسور بن مخرمة فذكراه. ومن طريقه رواه البيهقي في «الدلائل» (٤/١٩٧).

9026 — Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam and al-Miswar ibn Makhramah reported: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned during the year of al-Ḥudaybiyyah, and Sūrat al-Fatḥ was revealed to him between Makkah and Madinah. In it, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, granted him Khaybar: “Allah has promised you abundant spoils that you will obtain, and He has hastened this for you” [al-Fatḥ 48:20].
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ reached Madinah in Dhū al-Ḥijjah and remained there until he set out for Khaybar in Muḥarram. He camped at al-Rajīʿ, a valley between Khaybar and Ghaṭafān, fearing that Ghaṭafān might reinforce the people of Khaybar. He spent the night there and advanced against them the following morning.
Good: Narrated by Muḥammad ibn Isḥāq, who said: al-Zuhrī narrated to me, from ʿUrwah, from Marwān ibn al-Ḥakam and al-Miswar ibn Makhramah; through Ibn Isḥāq, al-Bayhaqī also narrated it in Dalāʾil al-Nubuwwah (4/197).

٩٠٢٧ — عن عراك بن مالك الغفاري أن أبا هريرة قدم المدينة في رهط من قومه، والنبي ﷺ بخيبر، وقد استخلف سباع بن عرفطة على المدينة.
قال: فانتهيت إليه وهو يقرأ في صلاة الصبح، في الركعة الأولى: ﴿كهيعص﴾ [مريم: ١]، وفي الثانية: ﴿وَيْلٌ لِلْمُطَفِّفِينَ﴾ [المطففين: ١].
قال: قلت لنفسي: ويل لفلان؛ إذا اكتال اكتال بالوافي، وإذا كال كال بالناقص.
قال: فلما صلى زودنا شيئًا حتى أتينا خيبر، وقد افتتح النبي ﷺ خيبر. فكلّم المسلمين، فأشركونا في سهامهم.
حسن: رواه أحمد (٨٥٥٢) والبزار في «كشف الأستار» (٢٢٨١)، وصححه ابن خزيمة (١٠٣٩) والحاكم (٢/٣٣) والبيهقي (٩/٤٠)، كلهم من حديث خثيم بن عراك، عن أبيه عراك، عن أبي هريرة فذكره.

english_source:
9027 — ʿIrāk ibn Mālik al-Ghifārī reported that Abū Hurayrah arrived in Madinah with a group from his tribe while the Prophet ﷺ was at Khaybar, having appointed Sibāʿ ibn ʿUrfuṭah as his deputy over Madinah.
Abū Hurayrah said: I reached him while he was leading the dawn prayer. In the first unit he recited: “Kāf Hā Yā ʿAyn Ṣād” [Maryam 19:1], and in the second: “Woe to those who give short measure” [al-Muṭaffifīn 83:1].
I said to myself, “Woe to so-and-so! When he receives a measure, he takes it in full, but when he gives a measure, he gives less.”
After the prayer, Sibāʿ provided us with some provisions, and we travelled to Khaybar. The Prophet ﷺ had already conquered it. He spoke to the Muslims on our behalf, and they allowed us to share in their allotted portions.
Good: Narrated by Aḥmad (8552) and al-Bazzār in Kashf al-Astār (2281), and authenticated by Ibn Khuzaymah (1039) and al-Ḥākim (2/33); al-Bayhaqī also narrated it (9/40), all through Khuthaym ibn ʿIrāk, from his father ʿIrāk, from Abū Hurayrah.

٩٠٢٨ — عن سويد بن النعمان أنه خرج مع النبي ﷺ عام خيبر، حتى إذا كنا بالصهباء، وهي من أدنى خيبر، صلى العصر، ثم دعا بالأزواد، فلم يؤت إلا بالسويق، فأمر به فثُرِّي، فأكل وأكلنا. ثم قام إلى المغرب، فمضمض ومضمضنا، ثم صلى ولم يتوضأ.
صحيح: رواه مالك في الطهارة (٥١) عن يحيى بن سعيد، عن بشير بن يسار مولى بني حارثة، عن سويد بن النعمان أنه أخبره قال: فذكره.

9028 — Suwayd ibn al-Nuʿmān reported that he went with the Prophet ﷺ during the year of Khaybar. When they reached al-Ṣahbāʾ, near Khaybar, the Prophet ﷺ performed the afternoon prayer and called for provisions. Nothing was brought except sawīq, a preparation of roasted grain. He ordered that it be moistened, and he and the Companions ate it. He then rose for the sunset prayer, rinsed his mouth, and the Companions did likewise. He prayed without renewing his ablution.
Authentic: Mālik related it in al-Ṭahārah (51) from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Bashīr ibn Yasār, the freedman of Banū Ḥārithah, from Suwayd ibn al-Nuʿmān, who related the report.
english_display:
9028 — Suwayd ibn al-Nuʿmān reported that he went with the Prophet ﷺ during the year of Khaybar. When they reached al-Ṣahbāʾ, near Khaybar, the Prophet ﷺ performed the afternoon prayer and called for provisions. Nothing was brought except sawīq, a preparation of roasted grain. He ordered that it be moistened, and he and the Companions ate it. He then rose for the sunset prayer, rinsed his mouth, and the Companions did likewise. He prayed without renewing his ablution.
Authentic: Mālik related it in al-Ṭahārah (51) from Yaḥyā ibn Saʿīd, from Bashīr ibn Yasār, the freedman of Banū Ḥārithah, from Suwayd ibn al-Nuʿmān, who related the report.

٩٠٢٨ — عن سويد بن النعمان أنه خرج مع النبي ﷺ عام خيبر، حتى إذا كنا بالصهباء، وهي من أدنى خيبر، صلى العصر، ثم دعا بالأزواد، فلم يؤت إلا بالسويق، فأمر به فثُرِّي، فأكل وأكلنا. ثم قام إلى المغرب، فمضمض ومضمضنا، ثم صلى ولم يتوضأ.
صحيح: رواه مالك في الطهارة (٥١) عن يحيى بن سعيد، عن بشير بن يسار مولى بني حارثة، عن سويد بن النعمان أنه أخبره قال: فذكره.

٩٠٢٩ — عن سلمة بن الأكوع قال: خرجنا مع النبي ﷺ إلى خيبر، فسرنا ليلًا. فقال رجل من القوم لعامر: يا عامر، ألا تسمعنا من هنيهاتك؟ وكان عامر رجلًا حدّاء، فنزل يحدو بالقوم يقول:
اللهم لولا أنت ما اهتدينا
 ولا تصدقنا ولا صلينا
 فاغفر فداءً لك ما اقتفينا
 وألقين سكينة علينا
 وثبت الأقدام إن لاقينا
 إنا إذا صيح بنا أبينا
 وبالصياح عولوا علينا
فقال رسول الله ﷺ: «مَنْ هَذَا السَّائِقُ؟». قالوا: عامر بن الأكوع. قال: «يَرْحَمُهُ اللهُ».
فقال رجل من القوم: وجبت يا نبي الله، لولا أمتعتنا به!
فأتينا خيبر، فحاصرناهم حتى أصابتنا مخمصة شديدة. ثم إن الله تعالى فتحها عليهم. فلما أمسى الناس مساء اليوم الذي فتحت عليهم، أوقدوا نيرانًا كثيرة.
فقال النبي ﷺ: «مَا هَذِهِ النِّيرَانُ؟ عَلَى أَيِّ شَيْءٍ تُوقِدُونَ؟». قالوا: على لحم. قال: «عَلَى أَيِّ لَحْمٍ؟». قالوا: لحم الحمر الإنسية.
قال النبي ﷺ: «أَهْرِيقُوهَا وَاكْسِرُوهَا». فقال رجل: يا رسول الله، أو نهريقها ونغسلها؟ قال: «أَوْ ذَاكَ».
فلما تصاف القوم كان سيف عامر قصيرًا، فتناول به ساق يهودي ليضربه، فرجع ذباب سيفه فأصاب عين ركبة عامر، فمات منه.
فلما قفلوا رآني رسول الله ﷺ وهو آخذ بيدي، فقال: «مَا لَكَ؟». قلت: فداك أبي وأمي، زعموا أن عامرًا حبط عمله.
قال النبي ﷺ: «كَذَبَ مَنْ قَالَهُ؛ إِنَّ لَهُ لَأَجْرَيْنِ» وجمع بين إصبعيه، «إِنَّهُ لَجَاهِدٌ مُجَاهِدٌ، قَلَّ عَرَبِيٌّ مَشَى بِهَا مِثْلُهُ».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري في المغازي (٤١٩٦)، ومسلم في الجهاد والسير (١٨٠٢)، كلاهما عن سلمة بن الأكوع فذكره.

9029 — Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ reported: We set out with the Prophet ﷺ for Khaybar and travelled by night. A man asked ʿĀmir, “ʿĀmir, will you not recite some of your verses for us?” ʿĀmir was a camel-driver who chanted rhythmically, so he began chanting:
O Allah, had You not guided us, we would not be guided,
 nor would we give charity or pray.
 Forgive, as a ransom for You, the sins we have committed;
 send tranquillity down upon us,
 and make our feet firm when we meet the enemy.
 When we are called to battle, we stand firm,
 though with cries they have summoned forces against us.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked: “Who is this driver?”
They replied, “ʿĀmir ibn al-Akwaʿ.”
He said: “May Allah have mercy upon him.”
A man among the company said, “His martyrdom has now become certain, Prophet of Allah. If only you had allowed us to enjoy his company longer!”
We reached Khaybar and besieged its people until we suffered severe hunger. Allah, Exalted, then granted us victory over them. On the evening of the day of conquest, the people lit many fires.
The Prophet ﷺ asked: “What are these fires? What are you cooking?”
They replied, “Meat.”
He asked: “What kind of meat?”
They replied, “The meat of domesticated donkeys.”
The Prophet ﷺ said: “Pour it away and break the pots.”
A man asked, “Messenger of Allah, may we pour it away and wash the pots instead?”
He replied: “You may do that.”
When the two forces formed their battle lines, ʿĀmir, whose sword was short, attempted to strike a Jewish man’s leg. The tip of his sword rebounded and struck the artery at his own knee, causing his death.
As the Muslims returned, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw me and took my hand. He asked: “What is troubling you?”
I replied, “May my father and mother be sacrificed for you! They claim that ʿĀmir’s deeds have become void.”
The Prophet ﷺ said: “Whoever said that has lied. He will receive a double reward”—and he joined two fingers together—“for he was one who strove and exerted himself. Few Arabs have walked the earth like him.”
Agreed upon: Al-Bukhārī related it in al-Maghāzī (4196) and Muslim in al-Jihād wa-l-Siyar (1802), both from Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ.

9030 — ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah: “Why do you not urge our mounts onward with your chanting?”
He replied, “I have abandoned composing poetry.”
ʿUmar said to him, “Listen and obey.” He then chanted:
O Allah, had You not guided us, we would not be guided,
 nor would we give charity or pray.
 Send tranquillity down upon us,
 and make our feet firm when we meet the enemy.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “O Allah, have mercy upon him.”
ʿUmar said, “It has become certain.”
Authentic: Al-Nasāʾī related it in al-Sunan al-Kubrā (8193) from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Mūsā ibn Aʿyan, from Ibn Idrīs, from Ismāʿīl, from Qays, from ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb.
The Prophet ﷺ set out for Khaybar with the Companions of al-Ḥudaybiyyah and did not permit those who had remained behind at al-Ḥudaybiyyah to accompany him, because Allah, Exalted, said:
“Those who remained behind will say when you set out to take the spoils, ‘Allow us to follow you.’ They wish to change the word of Allah. Say, ‘You will never follow us. Allah said so beforehand.’ They will say, ‘Rather, you envy us.’ In fact, they understand only a little” [al-Fatḥ 48:15].
Allah, Glorified and Exalted, promised the spoils of Khaybar exclusively to the people of al-Ḥudaybiyyah, without allowing the Bedouins who had remained behind to share in them. The words, “They wish to change the word of Allah” [al-Fatḥ 48:15], refer to the promise Allah had made to the people of al-Ḥudaybiyyah.

٩٠٣١ — عن عبد الله بن مغفل قال: كنا محاصري خيبر، فرمى إنسان بجراب فيه شحم، فنزوت لآخذه، فالتفت فإذا النبي ﷺ، فاستحييت.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري في المغازي (٤٢١٤) ومسلم في الجهاد (٧٢:١٧٧٢) كلاهما من طريق شعبة، حدثني حميد بن هلال، عن عبد الله بن مغفل قال: فذكره.

9031 — ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mughaffal reported: While we were besieging Khaybar, someone threw down a leather bag containing fat. I sprang forward to take it, but then turned and saw the Prophet ﷺ, so I felt embarrassed.
Agreed upon: Al-Bukhārī related it in al-Maghāzī (4214) and Muslim in al-Jihād (1772:72), both through Shuʿbah, from Ḥumayd ibn Hilāl, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Mughaffal.

٩٠٣٢ — عن أنس بن مالك قال: صلى النبي ﷺ قريبًا من خيبر بغلس، ثم قال: «اللهُ أَكْبَرُ، خَرِبَتْ خَيْبَرُ، إِنَّا إِذَا نَزَلْنَا بِسَاحَةِ قَوْمٍ فَسَاءَ صَبَاحُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ».
فخرجوا يسعون في السكك، فقتل النبي ﷺ المقاتلة وسبى الذرية. الحديث.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري في المغازي (٤٢٠٠) ومسلم في النكاح (٨٥:١٣٦٥) كلاهما من طريق حماد بن زيد، عن ثابت، عن أنس قال: فذكره.

9032 — Anas ibn Mālik reported: The Prophet ﷺ performed the dawn prayer near Khaybar while it was still dark, then said: “Allah is the Greatest! Khaybar is ruined. When we descend into the territory of a people, terrible is the morning of those who were warned.”
The inhabitants came running through the streets. The Prophet ﷺ killed their fighting men and took their women and children captive. The remainder of the report follows.

9033 — Anas reported: The Prophet ﷺ reached Khaybar early in the morning, as its people came out carrying their spades. When they saw him, they cried, “Muḥammad and the army! Muḥammad and the army!” They turned and ran toward the fortress.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ raised his hands, proclaimed Allah’s greatness three times and said: “Khaybar is ruined. When we descend into the territory of a people, terrible is the morning of those who were warned.”
We captured some domesticated donkeys that had come out of the settlement and cooked their meat. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and His Messenger forbid you to eat domesticated donkeys, for they are an impurity from the work of Satan.”
Authentic: Aḥmad related it (12086) from Sufyān ibn ʿUyaynah, from Ayyūb, from Muḥammad, from Anas. Al-Bukhārī also related it in al-Jihād (2991) and Muslim in al-Ṣayd wa-l-Dhabāʾiḥ (1940) through other routes from Ayyūb with some wording abridged.

صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٦٣٤٧) والطبراني في الكبير (٥/٩٩-١٠٠) كلاهما من حديث سعيد بن أبي عروبة، عن قتادة، عن أنس، عن أبي طلحة، فذكره.
9035 — Abū Ṭalḥah reported: When the Prophet of Allah ﷺ reached Khaybar in the morning, its people had taken their spades and gone out to their cultivated lands. When they saw the Prophet of Allah ﷺ with the army, they turned and fled.
The Prophet of Allah ﷺ said: “Allah is the Greatest! Allah is the Greatest! When we descend into the territory of a people, terrible is the morning of those who were warned.”
Authentic: Aḥmad (16347) and al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (5/99–100) both related it through Saʿīd ibn Abī ʿArūbah, from Qatādah, from Anas, from Abū Ṭalḥah.

9036 — Anas reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ campaigned against Khaybar. We performed the dawn prayer near it while it was still dark. The Prophet of Allah ﷺ mounted, and Abū Ṭalḥah mounted with me riding behind him.
The Prophet of Allah ﷺ rode rapidly through a narrow passage in Khaybar, and my knee touched his thigh. His lower garment shifted from his thigh, and I could see the whiteness of the Prophet’s ﷺ thigh.
When he entered the settlement, he said: “Allah is the Greatest! Khaybar is ruined. When we descend into the territory of a people, terrible is the morning of those who were warned.” He repeated it three times.
The inhabitants had gone out to their work and cried, “Muḥammad!” ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz said: Some of our companions added, “And the army!” We conquered Khaybar by force.
Agreed upon: Al-Bukhārī related it in al-Ṣalāh (371) and Muslim in al-Jihād wa-l-Siyar (1365:12), both through Ismāʿīl ibn ʿUlayyah, from ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz ibn Ṣuhayb, from Anas. This wording is Muslim’s; al-Bukhārī’s is longer.
Al-Khamīs means an army, so called because it is traditionally divided into five sections: the vanguard, the rearguard, the right and left wings, and the centre.

٩٠٣٧ — عن أنس قال: كنت ردف أبي طلحة يوم خيبر، وقدمي تمس قدم رسول الله ﷺ. فأتيناهم حين بزغت الشمس، وقد أخرجوا مواشيهم، وخرجوا بفؤوسهم ومكاتلهم ومرورهم، فقالوا: محمد والخميس!
فقال رسول الله ﷺ: «خَرِبَتْ خَيْبَرُ، إِنَّا إِذَا نَزَلْنَا بِسَاحَةِ قَوْمٍ فَسَاءَ صَبَاحُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ». قال: وهزمهم الله عز وجل.
ووقعت في سهم دحية جارية جميلة، فاشتراها رسول الله ﷺ بسبعة أرؤس، ثم دفعها إلى أم سليم تصنعها له وتهيئها، وأحسبه قال: وتعتد في بيتها، وهي صفية بنت حيي.
وجعل رسول الله ﷺ وليمتها التمر والأقط والسمن. فحُصت الأرض أفاحيص، وجيء بالأنطاع فوضعت فيها، وجيء بالأقط والسمن، فشبع الناس.
فقال الناس: لا ندري، أتزوجها أم اتخذها أم ولد؟ قالوا: إن حجبها فهي امرأته، وإن لم يحجبها فهي أم ولد.
فلما أراد أن يركب حجبها، فقعدت على عجز البعير، فعرفوا أنه قد تزوجها.
فلما دنوا من المدينة دفع رسول الله ﷺ ودفعنا. فعثرت الناقة العضباء، وندر رسول الله ﷺ وندرت، فقام فسترها.
وقد أشرفت النساء فقلن: أبعد الله اليهودية.
قال: قلت: يا أبا حمزة، أوقع رسول الله ﷺ؟ قال: إي والله، لقد وقع.
صحيح: رواه البخاري في المغازي (٤٢٠٠) ومسلم في النكاح (٨٧:١٣٦٥) كلاهما من طريق ثابت، عن أنس قال: فذكره. والسياق لمسلم، وسياق البخاري مختصر، إلا أنه ذكره في مواضع كثيرة.

english_source:
9037 — Anas reported: On the day of Khaybar, I rode behind Abū Ṭalḥah, and my foot touched the foot of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. We reached the inhabitants just as the sun rose. They had brought out their livestock and gone out carrying axes, baskets and spades. They cried, “Muḥammad and the army!”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Khaybar is ruined. When we descend into the territory of a people, terrible is the morning of those who were warned.” Allah, Mighty and Majestic, defeated them.
A beautiful captive woman fell to the share of Diḥyah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ acquired her in exchange for seven captives and entrusted her to Umm Sulaym to prepare her for him. I believe he also said that she was to observe her waiting period in Umm Sulaym’s house. She was Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ held her wedding feast with dates, dried curds and clarified butter. Hollows were dug in the ground and leather sheets were spread within them. The dried curds and butter were brought, and the people ate their fill.
The people said, “We do not know whether he has married her or taken her as a bondwoman who may bear him a child. If he screens her, she is his wife; if he does not, she is a bondwoman.”
When he prepared to depart, he screened her, and she sat upon the rear of the camel. They therefore knew that he had married her.
As they approached Madinah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ urged his mount forward, and we did likewise. Al-ʿAḍbāʾ stumbled, throwing both the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Ṣafiyyah. He immediately stood and covered her.
The women looked on and said, “May Allah keep the Jewish woman far away!”
The narrator said: I asked, “Abū Ḥamzah, did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ really fall?”
He replied, “Yes, by Allah, he did.”
Authentic: Al-Bukhārī related it in al-Maghāzī (4200) and Muslim in al-Nikāḥ (1365:87), both through Thābit, from Anas. This wording is Muslim’s; al-Bukhārī’s is abridged, though he records it in many places.

٩٠٣٧ — عن أنس قال: كنت ردف أبي طلحة يوم خيبر، وقدمي تمس قدم رسول الله ﷺ. فأتيناهم حين بزغت الشمس، وقد أخرجوا مواشيهم، وخرجوا بفؤوسهم ومكاتلهم ومرورهم، فقالوا: محمد والخميس!
فقال رسول الله ﷺ: «خَرِبَتْ خَيْبَرُ، إِنَّا إِذَا نَزَلْنَا بِسَاحَةِ قَوْمٍ فَسَاءَ صَبَاحُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ». قال: وهزمهم الله عز وجل.
ووقعت في سهم دحية جارية جميلة، فاشتراها رسول الله ﷺ بسبعة أرؤس، ثم دفعها إلى أم سليم تصنعها له وتهيئها، وأحسبه قال: وتعتد في بيتها، وهي صفية بنت حيي.
وجعل رسول الله ﷺ وليمتها التمر والأقط والسمن. فحُصت الأرض أفاحيص، وجيء بالأنطاع فوضعت فيها، وجيء بالأقط والسمن، فشبع الناس.
فقال الناس: لا ندري، أتزوجها أم اتخذها أم ولد؟ قالوا: إن حجبها فهي امرأته، وإن لم يحجبها فهي أم ولد.
فلما أراد أن يركب حجبها، فقعدت على عجز البعير، فعرفوا أنه قد تزوجها.
فلما دنوا من المدينة دفع رسول الله ﷺ ودفعنا. فعثرت الناقة العضباء، وندر رسول الله ﷺ وندرت، فقام فسترها.
وقد أشرفت النساء فقلن: أبعد الله اليهودية.
قال: قلت: يا أبا حمزة، أوقع رسول الله ﷺ؟ قال: إي والله، لقد وقع.

9037 — Anas reported: On the day of Khaybar, I rode behind Abū Ṭalḥah, and my foot touched the foot of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. We reached the inhabitants just as the sun rose. They had brought out their livestock and gone out carrying axes, baskets and spades. They cried, “Muḥammad and the army!”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Khaybar is ruined. When we descend into the territory of a people, terrible is the morning of those who were warned.” Allah, Mighty and Majestic, defeated them.
A beautiful captive woman fell to the share of Diḥyah. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ acquired her in exchange for seven captives and entrusted her to Umm Sulaym to prepare her for him. I believe he also said that she was to observe her waiting period in Umm Sulaym’s house. She was Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ held her wedding feast with dates, dried curds and clarified butter. Hollows were dug in the ground and leather sheets were spread within them. The dried curds and butter were brought, and the people ate their fill.

When he prepared to depart, he screened her, and she sat upon the rear of the camel. They therefore knew that he had married her.
As they approached Madinah, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ urged his mount forward, and we did likewise. Al-ʿAḍbāʾ stumbled, throwing both the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Ṣafiyyah. He immediately stood and covered her.
The women looked on and said, “May Allah keep the Jewish woman far away!”
The narrator said: I asked, “Abū Ḥamzah, did the Messenger of Allah ﷺ really fall?”
He replied, “Yes, by Allah, he did.”

٩٠٣٨ — عن أنس بن مالك أن رسول الله ﷺ أتى خيبر ليلًا، وكان إذا أتى قومًا بليل لم يُغِر بهم حتى يصبح.
فلما أصبح خرجت اليهود بمساحيهم ومكاتلهم. فلما رأوه قالوا: محمد، والله! محمد والخميس!
فقال النبي ﷺ: «خَرِبَتْ خَيْبَرُ، إِنَّا إِذَا نَزَلْنَا بِسَاحَةِ قَوْمٍ فَسَاءَ صَبَاحُ الْمُنْذَرِينَ».
صحيح: رواه مالك في الجهاد (٤٨) عن حميد الطويل، عن أنس قال: فذكره. ورواه البخاري في المغازي (٤١٩٧) عن عبد الله بن يوسف، أخبرنا مالك، به مثله.

٩٠٣٩ — عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال: لما غزا رسول الله ﷺ خيبر، أو قال: لما توجه رسول الله ﷺ، أشرف الناس على واد، فرفعوا أصواتهم بالتكبير: الله أكبر، الله أكبر، لا إله إلا الله.
فقال رسول الله ﷺ: «ارْبَعُوا عَلَى أَنْفُسِكُمْ؛ إِنَّكُمْ لَا تَدْعُونَ أَصَمَّ وَلَا غَائِبًا، إِنَّكُمْ تَدْعُونَ سَمِيعًا قَرِيبًا، وَهُوَ مَعَكُمْ».
وأنا خلف دابة رسول الله ﷺ، فسمعني وأنا أقول: لا حول ولا قوة إلا بالله.
فقال لي: «يَا عَبْدَ اللهِ بْنَ قَيْسٍ». قلت: لبيك يا رسول الله. قال: «أَلَا أَدُلُّكَ عَلَى كَلِمَةٍ مِنْ كَنْزٍ مِنْ كُنُوزِ الْجَنَّةِ؟». قلت: بلى يا رسول الله، فداك أبي وأمي. قال: «لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللهِ».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري في المغازي (٤٢٠٢) ومسلم في الذكر والدعاء (٤٤:٢٧٠٤) كلاهما من طريق عاصم (هو الأحول) عن أبي عثمان (هو النهدي) عن أبي موسى قال: فذكره.

9039 — Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī reported: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ campaigned against Khaybar—or when he set out toward it—the people overlooked a valley and raised their voices, proclaiming: “Allah is the Greatest! Allah is the Greatest! There is no deity worthy of worship except Allah!”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “Be gentle with yourselves. You are not calling upon one who is deaf or absent. You are calling upon One who hears and is near, and He is with you.”
I was behind the mount of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he heard me saying, “There is no power or might except through Allah.”
He said: “ʿAbd Allāh ibn Qays.”
I replied, “At your service, Messenger of Allah.”
He asked: “Shall I direct you to a phrase from one of the treasures of Paradise?”
I replied, “Yes, Messenger of Allah; may my father and mother be sacrificed for you.”
He said: “‘There is no power or might except through Allah.’”
Agreed upon: Al-Bukhārī related it in al-Maghāzī (4202) and Muslim in al-Dhikr wa-l-Duʿāʾ (2704:44), both through ʿĀṣim al-Aḥwal, from Abū ʿUthmān al-Nahdī, from Abū Mūsā.

٩٠٤٠ — عن سلمة بن الأكوع قال: كان علي رضي الله عنه تخلف عن النبي ﷺ في خيبر، وكان رمدًا. فقال: أنا أتخلف عن النبي ﷺ؟ فلحق به.
فلما بتنا الليلة التي فتحت، قال: «لَأُعْطِيَنَّ الرَّايَةَ غَدًا، أَوْ لَيَأْخُذَنَّ الرَّايَةَ غَدًا، رَجُلٌ يُحِبُّهُ اللهُ وَرَسُولُهُ، يُفْتَحُ عَلَيْهِ».
فنحن نرجوها، فقيل: هذا علي. فأعطاه، ففتح عليه.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري في المغازي (٤٢٠٩) ومسلم في فضائل الصحابة (٣٥:٢٤٠٧) كلاهما من طريق هاشم (هو ابن إسماعيل) عن يزيد بن أبي عبيد، عن سلمة بن الأكوع قال: فذكره.

9040 — Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ reported: ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, initially remained behind when the Prophet ﷺ went to Khaybar because he was suffering from inflamed eyes. He then said, “Should I remain behind the Prophet ﷺ?” and caught up with him.
On the night before the conquest, the Prophet ﷺ said: “Tomorrow I shall certainly give the banner—or the banner will certainly be taken—by a man whom Allah and His Messenger love, and victory will be granted through him.”
We all hoped to receive it, but then it was said, “Here is ʿAlī.” The Prophet ﷺ gave him the banner, and victory was granted through him.
Agreed upon: Al-Bukhārī related it in al-Maghāzī (4209) and Muslim in Faḍāʾil al-Ṣaḥābah (2407:35), both through Hāshim ibn Ismāʿīl, from Yazīd ibn Abī ʿUbayd, from Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ.

٩٠٤١ — عن سهل بن سعد أن رسول الله ﷺ قال يوم خيبر: «لَأُعْطِيَنَّ هَذِهِ الرَّايَةَ غَدًا رَجُلًا يَفْتَحُ اللهُ عَلَى يَدَيْهِ، يُحِبُّ اللهَ وَرَسُولَهُ، وَيُحِبُّهُ اللهُ وَرَسُولُهُ».
فبات الناس يدوكون ليلتهم: أيهم يعطاها؟ فلما أصبح الناس غدوا على رسول الله ﷺ، كلهم يرجو أن يعطاها.
فقال: «أَيْنَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ؟». فقيل: هو يا رسول الله يشتكي عينيه. قال: «فَأَرْسِلُوا إِلَيْهِ».
فأتي به، فبصق رسول الله ﷺ في عينيه ودعا له، فبرأ حتى كأن لم يكن به وجع، فأعطاه الراية.
فقال علي: يا رسول الله، أقاتلهم حتى يكونوا مثلنا؟
فقال: «انْفُذْ عَلَى رِسْلِكَ حَتَّى تَنْزِلَ بِسَاحَتِهِمْ، ثُمَّ ادْعُهُمْ إِلَى الْإِسْلَامِ، وَأَخْبِرْهُمْ بِمَا يَجِبُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنْ حَقِّ اللهِ فِيهِ. فَوَاللهِ لَأَنْ يَهْدِيَ اللهُ بِكَ رَجُلًا وَاحِدًا خَيْرٌ لَكَ مِنْ أَنْ يَكُونَ لَكَ حُمْرُ النَّعَمِ».
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري في المغازي (٤٢١٠) ومسلم في فضائل الصحابة (٣٤:٢٤٠٦) كلاهما عن قتيبة بن سعيد، حدثنا يعقوب بن عبد الرحمن، عن أبي حازم، قال: أخبرني سهل بن سعد فذكره.

9041 — Sahl ibn Saʿd reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said on the day of Khaybar: “Tomorrow I shall give this banner to a man through whose hands Allah will grant victory. He loves Allah and His Messenger, and Allah and His Messenger love him.”
The people spent the night discussing which of them would receive it. The following morning, they all went early to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, each hoping to be given the banner.
He asked: “Where is ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib?”
They replied, “Messenger of Allah, his eyes are hurting.”
He said: “Send for him.”
ʿAlī was brought, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ spat into his eyes and supplicated for him. He was cured as though he had never suffered any pain, and the Prophet ﷺ gave him the banner.
ʿAlī asked, “Messenger of Allah, shall I fight them until they become like us?”
He replied: “Proceed calmly until you reach their territory. Then invite them to Islam and inform them of the rights of Allah that become binding upon them within it. By Allah, for Allah to guide one man through you is better for you than possessing the finest red camels.”
Agreed upon: Al-Bukhārī related it in al-Maghāzī (4210) and Muslim in Faḍāʾil al-Ṣaḥābah (2406:34), both from Qutaybah ibn Saʿīd, from Yaʿqūb ibn ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Abū Ḥāzim, from Sahl ibn Saʿd.

٩٠٤١ — عن سهل بن سعد أن رسول الله ﷺ قال يوم خيبر: «لَأُعْطِيَنَّ هَذِهِ الرَّايَةَ غَدًا رَجُلًا يَفْتَحُ اللهُ عَلَى يَدَيْهِ، يُحِبُّ اللهَ وَرَسُولَهُ، وَيُحِبُّهُ اللهُ وَرَسُولُهُ».
فبات الناس يدوكون ليلتهم: أيهم يعطاها؟ فلما أصبح الناس غدوا على رسول الله ﷺ، كلهم يرجو أن يعطاها.
فقال: «أَيْنَ عَلِيُّ بْنُ أَبِي طَالِبٍ؟». فقيل: هو يا رسول الله يشتكي عينيه. قال: «فَأَرْسِلُوا إِلَيْهِ».
فأتي به، فبصق رسول الله ﷺ في عينيه ودعا له، فبرأ حتى كأن لم يكن به وجع، فأعطاه الراية.

٩٠٤٤ — عن سلمة بن الأكوع قال: فذكر حديثًا طويلًا، وفيه: فوالله ما لبثنا إلا ثلاث ليال حتى خرجنا إلى خيبر مع رسول الله ﷺ. قال: فجعل عمي عامر يرتجز بالقوم:
تالله لولا الله ما اهتدينا
 ولا تصدقنا ولا صلينا
 ونحن عن فضلك ما استغنينا

9044 — Salamah ibn al-Akwaʿ related a lengthy report containing the following:
By Allah, we remained only three nights before setting out for Khaybar with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. My uncle ʿĀmir began chanting to the company:
By Allah, had Allah not guided us, we would not be guided,
 nor would we give charity or pray.
 We can never dispense with Your favour;
 make our feet firm when we meet the enemy,
 and send tranquillity down upon us.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked: “Who is this?”
He replied, “I am ʿĀmir.”
He said: “May your Lord forgive you.”
Whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ specifically prayed for someone’s forgiveness in this manner, that person attained martyrdom. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, who was riding a camel, called out, “Prophet of Allah, if only you had allowed us to enjoy ʿĀmir’s company longer!”
When we reached Khaybar, their champion Marḥab came out, strutting with his sword and chanting:
Khaybar knows that I am Marḥab,
 fully armed, a tested warrior,
 when wars advance in blazing fury.
My uncle ʿĀmir came out against him and chanted:
Khaybar knows that I am ʿĀmir,
 fully armed, a daring warrior.
They exchanged two blows. Marḥab’s sword struck ʿĀmir’s shield, and ʿĀmir attempted to strike him from below. His sword rebounded upon himself and severed the artery in his forearm, causing his death.
Salamah said: I came upon several Companions of the Prophet ﷺ saying, “ʿĀmir’s deeds have become void; he killed himself.”
I went to the Prophet ﷺ weeping and asked, “Messenger of Allah, have ʿĀmir’s deeds become void?”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked: “Who said that?”
I replied, “Some of your Companions.”
He said: “Whoever said that has lied. Rather, he will receive a double reward.”
He then sent me to fetch ʿAlī, who was suffering from inflamed eyes, saying: “I shall give the banner to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger—or whom Allah and His Messenger love.”
I went to ʿAlī and led him by the hand because of his eyes until I brought him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He spat into his eyes, and they were cured. He then gave him the banner.
Marḥab came out chanting:
Khaybar knows that I am Marḥab,
 fully armed, a tested warrior,
 when wars advance in blazing fury.
ʿAlī replied:
I am the one whose mother named him Ḥaydarah,
 like a lion of the forests, fearsome to behold;
 I repay them measure for measure, in a mighty measure.
ʿAlī struck Marḥab on the head and killed him, and victory was then achieved at his hands.
Authentic: Muslim related it in al-Jihād wa-l-Siyar (1807:132) through ʿIkrimah ibn ʿAmmār, from Iyās ibn Salamah, from his father. The report is given in full in the al-Ḥudaybiyyah section.

I went to ʿAlī and led him by the hand because of his eyes until I brought him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He spat into his eyes, and they were cured. He then gave him the banner.
Marḥab came out chanting:
Khaybar knows that I am Marḥab,
 fully armed, a tested warrior,
 when wars advance in blazing fury.
ʿAlī replied:
I am the one whose mother named him Ḥaydarah,
 like a lion of the forests, fearsome to behold;
 I repay them measure for measure, in a mighty measure.
ʿAlī struck Marḥab on the head and killed him, and victory was then achieved at his hands.
Authentic: Muslim related it in al-Jihād wa-l-Siyar (1807:132) through ʿIkrimah ibn ʿAmmār, from Iyās ibn Salamah, from his father. The report is given in full in the al-Ḥudaybiyyah section.

٩٠٤٦ — عن ابن عمر قال: لما افتتحت خيبر، سألت يهود رسول الله ﷺ أن يقرهم فيها على أن يعملوا على نصف ما خرج منها من الثمر والزرع.
فقال رسول الله ﷺ: «أُقِرُّكُمْ فِيهَا عَلَى ذَلِكَ مَا شِئْنَا».
وفيه: وكان الثمر يقسم على السهمان من نصف خيبر، فيأخذ رسول الله ﷺ الخمس.
صحيح: رواه مسلم في المساقاة (٤:١٥٥١) عن أبي الطاهر، حدثنا عبد الله بن وهب، أخبرني أسامة بن زيد، عن نافع، عن عبد الله بن عمر فذكره.

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We shall allow you to remain upon these terms for as long as we wish.”
The report also states that the produce from half of Khaybar was distributed according to the allotted shares, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took one-fifth.

٩٠٤٧ — عن ابن عمر أن عمر بن الخطاب أجلى اليهود والنصارى من أرض الحجاز. وكان رسول الله ﷺ لما ظهر على خيبر أراد إخراج اليهود منها، وكانت الأرض حين ظهر عليها لله ولرسوله وللمسلمين.
وأراد إخراج اليهود منها، فسألت اليهود رسول الله ﷺ أن يقرهم بها، على أن يكفوا عملها ولهم نصف الثمر.
فقال رسول الله ﷺ: «نُقِرُّكُمْ بِهَا عَلَى ذَلِكَ مَا شِئْنَا». فقروا بها حتى أجلاهم عمر إلى تيماء وأريحاء.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري في الحرث والمزارعة (٢٣٣٨) ومسلم في المساقاة (٦:١٥٥١) كلاهما من حديث عبد الرزاق، أخبرنا ابن جريج، حدثني موسى بن عقبة، عن نافع، عن ابن عمر فذكره.

9047 — Ibn ʿUmar reported that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb expelled the Jews and Christians from the land of the Ḥijāz.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ conquered Khaybar, he intended to expel its Jewish inhabitants. Upon its conquest, the land belonged to Allah, His Messenger and the Muslims. When the Prophet ﷺ sought to remove them, they asked him to allow them to remain and perform its agricultural work in return for half the produce.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: “We shall allow you to remain upon these terms for as long as we wish.”
They remained there until ʿUmar expelled them to Taymāʾ and Jericho.
Agreed upon: Al-Bukhārī related it in al-Ḥarth wa-l-Muzāraʿah (2338) and Muslim in al-Musāqāh (1551:6), both through ʿAbd al-Razzāq, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mūsā ibn ʿUqbah, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar.

arabic_source:
٩٠٤٨ — عن ابن عمر قال: لما فدع أهل خيبر عبد الله بن عمر، قام عمر خطيبًا فقال: إن رسول الله ﷺ كان عامل يهود خيبر على أموالهم، وقال: «نُقِرُّكُمْ مَا أَقَرَّكُمُ اللهُ».
وإن عبد الله بن عمر خرج إلى ماله هناك، فعُدي عليه من الليل، ففُدعت يداه ورجلاه. وليس لنا هناك عدو غيرهم؛ هم عدونا وتهمتنا، وقد رأيت إجلاءهم.
فلما أجمع عمر على ذلك أتاه أحد بني أبي الحقيق فقال: يا أمير المؤمنين، أتخرجنا وقد أقرنا محمد ﷺ وعاملنا على الأموال وشرط ذلك لنا؟
فقال عمر: أظننت أني نسيت قول رسول الله ﷺ: «كَيْفَ بِكَ إِذَا أُخْرِجْتَ مِنْ خَيْبَرَ، تَعْدُو بِكَ قَلُوصُكَ لَيْلَةً بَعْدَ لَيْلَةٍ؟».
فقال: كانت هذه هزيلة من أبي القاسم. قال: كذبت يا عدو الله.
فأجلاهم عمر، وأعطاهم قيمة ما كان لهم من الثمر مالًا وإبلًا وعروضًا من أقتاب وحبال وغير ذلك.
صحيح: رواه البخاري (٢٧٣٠).

“The Messenger of Allah ﷺ contracted with the Jewish inhabitants of Khaybar concerning their lands and said: ‘We shall allow you to remain for as long as Allah allows you to remain.’

٩٠٤٩ — عن ابن عمر أن رسول الله ﷺ قاتل أهل خيبر حتى ألجأهم إلى قصرهم، فغلب على الأرض والزرع والنخل. فصالحوه على أن يجلوا منها، ولهم ما حملت ركابهم، ولرسول الله ﷺ الصفراء والبيضاء، ويخرجون منها.
فاشترط عليهم ألا يكتموا ولا يغيّبوا شيئًا، فإن فعلوا فلا ذمة لهم. فغيّبوا مَسْكًا فيه مال وحلي لحيي بن أخطب، كان احتمله معه إلى خيبر حين أُجليت النضير.
فقال رسول الله ﷺ لعم حيي بن أخطب: «مَا فَعَلَ مَسْكُ حُيَيٍّ الَّذِي جَاءَ بِهِ مِنَ النَّضِيرِ؟». قال: أذهبته النفقات والحروب.
فقال: «الْعَهْدُ قَرِيبٌ، وَالْمَالُ أَكْثَرُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ». فدفعه رسول الله ﷺ إلى الزبير، فمسه بعذاب. وقد كان قبل ذلك دخل خربة، فقال: قد رأيت حييًّا يطوف في خربة هاهنا. فذهبوا فطافوا، فوجدوا المسك في الخربة.
فقتل رسول الله ﷺ ابني أبي الحقيق، وأحدهما زوج صفية بنت حيي بن أخطب. وسبى رسول الله ﷺ نساءهم وذراريهم، وقسم أموالهم للنكث الذي نكثوا.
وأراد أن يجليهم منها، فقالوا: يا محمد، دعنا نكون في هذه الأرض نصلحها ونقوم عليها. ولم يكن لرسول الله ﷺ ولا لأصحابه غلمان يقومون عليها، وكانوا لا يتفرغون أن يقوموا عليها.
فأعطاهم خيبر على أن لهم الشطر من كل زرع ونخل وشيء، ما بدا لرسول الله ﷺ.
وكان عبد الله بن رواحة يأتيهم كل عام فيخرصها، ثم يضمنهم الشطر. فشكوا إلى رسول الله ﷺ في عام شدة خرصه، وأرادوا أن يرشوه.
فقال: يا أعداء الله، أتطعمونني السحت؟ ولقد جئتكم من عند أحب الناس إلي، ولأنتم أبغض إلي من عدتكم من القردة والخنازير، ولا يحملني بغضي إياكم وحبي إياه على ألا أعدل عليكم.
فقالوا: بهذا قامت السماوات والأرض.
قال: ورأى رسول الله ﷺ بعيني صفية خضرة، فقال: «مَا هَذِهِ الْخُضْرَةُ بِعَيْنَيْكِ؟».
قالت: كان رأسي في حجر ابن أبي الحقيق وأنا نائمة، فرأيت كأن قمرًا وقع في حجري. فأخبرته بذلك، فلطمني وقال: تمنّين ملك يثرب؟
قالت: وكان رسول الله ﷺ من أبغض الناس إلي؛ قتل زوجي وأبي وأخي. فما زال يعتذر إلي ويقول: «إِنَّ أَبَاكِ أَلَّبَ عَلَيَّ الْعَرَبَ، وَفَعَلَ وَفَعَلَ»، حتى ذهب ذلك من نفسي.
وكان رسول الله ﷺ يعطي كل امرأة من نسائه ثمانين وسقًا من تمر كل عام وعشرين وسقًا من شعير.
فلما كان زمن عمر بن الخطاب غشوا المسلمين، وألقوا ابن عمر من فوق بيت. فقال عمر بن الخطاب: من كان له سهم من خيبر فليحضر حتى نقسمها بينهم. فقسمها عمر بينهم.
فقال رئيسهم: لا تخرجنا، دعنا نكون فيها كما أقرنا رسول الله ﷺ وأبو بكر.
فقال عمر لرئيسهم: أتراه سقط عني قول رسول الله ﷺ لك: «كَيْفَ بِكَ إِذَا أَفْضَتْ بِكَ رَاحِلَتُكَ نَحْوَ الشَّامِ يَوْمًا ثُمَّ يَوْمًا؟».
وقسمها عمر بين من كان شهد خيبر من أهل الحديبية.
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٣٠٠٦)، وصححه ابن حبان (٥١٩٩)، والبيهقي في «السنن» (١٣٧-١٣٨/٩).

9049 — Ibn ʿUmar reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ fought the people of Khaybar until he drove them into their fortress and gained control of their land, crops and date palms. They concluded a treaty with him stipulating that they would leave Khaybar, taking only what their mounts could carry, while all their gold and silver would belong to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
He stipulated that they must neither conceal nor hide anything; if they did, they would no longer enjoy covenantal protection. They nevertheless concealed a leather bag containing the wealth and jewellery of Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab, which he had brought to Khaybar when Banū al-Naḍīr were expelled.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab’s uncle: “What happened to Ḥuyayy’s leather bag that he brought from al-Naḍīr?”
He replied, “Expenses and warfare consumed its contents.”
The Prophet ﷺ said: “The time has been too short, and the wealth was too great for that.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ handed him over to al-Zubayr, who subjected him to physical pressure during interrogation. The man had previously entered a ruined building, so he said, “I saw Ḥuyayy moving around a ruin over here.” They searched the place and found the leather bag in the ruin.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ executed the two sons of Abū al-Ḥuqayq, one of whom was the husband of Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab. Because they had violated the agreement, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took their women and children captive and divided their property.
He intended to expel them from Khaybar, but they said, “Muḥammad, allow us to remain upon this land to cultivate and maintain it.” Neither the Messenger of Allah ﷺ nor his Companions had sufficient workers to maintain the land, nor were they free to undertake the work themselves.
He therefore allowed the people of Khaybar to remain on the condition that they receive half of every crop, date harvest and other produce, for as long as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wished.
ʿAbd Allāh ibn Rawāḥah used to visit them every year, estimate the harvest and make them liable for half. One year they complained to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ about the strictness of his assessment and attempted to bribe him.
He said, “Enemies of Allah, would you feed me unlawful gain? I have come to you from the person dearest to me, while you are more hateful to me than an equivalent number of apes and swine. Yet neither my hatred of you nor my love for him will cause me to act unjustly toward you.”
They replied, “It is through such justice that the heavens and earth remain established.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ noticed a greenish bruise around Ṣafiyyah’s eyes and asked: “What is this mark around your eyes?”
She replied, “My head was resting in the lap of Ibn Abī al-Ḥuqayq while I slept, and I dreamed that the moon fell into my lap. When I told him, he struck me and said, ‘Do you desire the king of Yathrib?’”
She said: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was initially the most hateful of people to me, for my husband, father and brother had been killed. He continued explaining the circumstances to me, saying, ‘Your father incited the Arabs against me and did such-and-such,’ until those feelings left my heart.”
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to give each of his wives eighty wasqs of dates and twenty wasqs of barley every year.
During the caliphate of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, the people of Khaybar acted treacherously toward the Muslims and threw Ibn ʿUmar from the roof of a house. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said, “Whoever possesses a share in Khaybar should attend so that we may distribute it among them.” He then divided it among its Muslim shareholders.
Their leader said, “Do not expel us. Allow us to remain as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Abū Bakr allowed us to remain.”
ʿUmar said to him, “Do you imagine that I have forgotten the Messenger of Allah’s ﷺ words to you: ‘What will your condition be when your mount carries you toward Syria, one day after another?’”
ʿUmar then divided Khaybar among the people of al-Ḥudaybiyyah who had participated in its conquest.
Authentic: Related by Abū Dāwūd (3006), authenticated by Ibn Ḥibbān (5199), and related by al-Bayhaqī in al-Sunan (9/137–138).

٩٠٥٠ — عن عبد الله بن عمر قال: خرجت أنا والزبير والمقداد بن الأسود إلى أموالنا بخيبر لنتعاهدها. فلما قدمناها تفرقنا في أموالنا.
قال: فعُدي عليَّ تحت الليل وأنا نائم على فراشي، ففُدعت يداي من مرفقي.
فلما أصبحت استُصرخ عليَّ صاحباي، فأتياني فسألاني: من صنع هذا بك؟ قلت: لا أدري. فأصلحا من يديَّ، ثم قدموا بي على عمر.
فقال: هذا عمل يهود.
ثم قام في الناس خطيبًا فقال: أيها الناس، إن رسول الله ﷺ كان عامل يهود خيبر على أنا نخرجهم إذا شئنا. وقد عدوا على عبد الله بن عمر، ففدعوا يديه كما بلغكم، مع عدوهم على الأنصاري قبله. لا نشك أنهم أصحابه؛ ليس لنا هناك عدو غيرهم.
فمن كان له مال بخيبر فليلحق به، فإني مخرج يهود. فأخرجهم.
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٣٠٠٧) عن الإمام أحمد وهو في مسنده (٩٠) عن يعقوب بن إبراهيم حدثنا أبي، عن ابن إسحاق، حدثني نافع مولى عبد الله بن عمر، عن عبد الله بن عمر فذكره، واللفظ لأحمد، وأما أبو داود فاختصره.

٩٠٥١ — عن ابن عمر قال: قسم رسول الله ﷺ يوم خيبر للفرس سهمين، وللراجل سهمًا.
قال: فسره نافع فقال: إذا كان مع الرجل فرس فله ثلاثة أسهم، فإن لم يكن له فرس فله سهم.
صحيح: رواه البخاري في المغازي (٤٢٢٨) ومسلم في الجهاد والسير (٥٧:١٧٦٢) كلاهما من طريق عبيد الله بن عمر، عن نافع، عن ابن عمر قال: فذكره. والسياق للبخاري، وليس في مسلم قول عبيد الله.

9051 — Ibn ʿUmar reported: On the day of Khaybar, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ allotted two shares for a horse and one share for a foot soldier.
Nāfiʿ explained: A man who possessed a horse received three shares—two for the horse and one for himself. A man without a horse received one share.
Authentic: Al-Bukhārī related it in al-Maghāzī (4228) and Muslim in al-Jihād wa-l-Siyar (1762:57), both through ʿUbayd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, from Nāfiʿ, from Ibn ʿUmar. The wording is al-Bukhārī’s.

٩٠٥٢ — عن جبير بن مطعم قال: مشيت أنا وعثمان بن عفان إلى النبي ﷺ فقلنا: أعطيت بني المطلب من خمس خيبر، وتركتنا ونحن بمنزلة واحدة منك؟
فقال: «إِنَّمَا بَنُو هَاشِمٍ وَبَنُو الْمُطَّلِبِ شَيْءٌ وَاحِدٌ».
قال جبير: ولم يقسم النبي ﷺ لبني عبد شمس وبني نوفل شيئًا.
صحيح: رواه البخاري في المغازي (٤٢٢٩) عن يحيى بن بكير، حدثنا الليث، عن يونس، عن ابن شهاب، عن سعيد بن المسيب، أن جبير بن مطعم أخبره فذكره.

9052 — Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim reported: ʿUthmān ibn ʿAffān and I went to the Prophet ﷺ and said, “You gave Banū al-Muṭṭalib a share from the one-fifth of Khaybar but gave us nothing, even though our degree of kinship to you is the same.”
He replied: “Banū Hāshim and Banū al-Muṭṭalib are one and the same.”
Jubayr said: The Prophet ﷺ did not allot anything to Banū ʿAbd Shams or Banū Nawfal.
Authentic: Al-Bukhārī related it in al-Maghāzī (4229) from Yaḥyā ibn Bukayr, from al-Layth, from Yūnus, from Ibn Shihāb, from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib, from Jubayr ibn Muṭʿim.

٩٠٥٣ — عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال: قدمنا على النبي ﷺ بعد أن افتتح خيبر، فقسم لنا، ولم يقسم لأحد لم يشهد الفتح غيرنا.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٢٣٣)، ومسلم (١٦٩:٢٥٠٢).
قوله: «ولم يقسم لأحد لم يشهد الفتح غيرنا»: أراد أبو موسى أنه لم يسهم لأحد لم يشهد الوقعة من غير استرضاء أحد من الغانمين إلا لأصحاب السفينة. وأما أبو هريرة وأصحابه فلم يعطهم إلا عن طيب خواطر المسلمين. «فتح الباري» (٤٨٩/٧).

9053 — Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī reported: We came to the Prophet ﷺ after he had conquered Khaybar. He allotted shares to us, although he gave no share to anyone else who had not witnessed the conquest.
Agreed upon: Related by al-Bukhārī (4233) and Muslim (2502:169).
Regarding the words, “He gave no share to anyone else who had not witnessed the conquest,” Abū Mūsā meant that, apart from the people of the ship, no absent person received a formal share without the consent of those who had acquired the spoils. Abū Hurayrah and his companions were given something only with the willing approval of the Muslims. See Fatḥ al-Bārī (7/489).

Agreed upon: Related by al-Bukhārī (4233) and Muslim (2502:169).
Regarding the words, “He gave no share to anyone else who had not witnessed the conquest,” Abū Mūsā meant that, apart from the people of the ship, no absent person received a formal share without the consent of those who had acquired the spoils. Abū Hurayrah and his companions were given something only with the willing approval of the Muslims. See Fatḥ al-Bārī (7/489).

٩٠٥٣ — عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال: قدمنا على النبي ﷺ بعد أن افتتح خيبر، فقسم لنا، ولم يقسم لأحد لم يشهد الفتح غيرنا.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري (٤٢٣٣)، ومسلم (١٦٩:٢٥٠٢).
قوله: «ولم يقسم لأحد لم يشهد الفتح غيرنا»: أراد أبو موسى أنه لم يسهم لأحد لم يشهد الوقعة من غير استرضاء أحد من الغانمين إلا لأصحاب السفينة. وأما أبو هريرة وأصحابه فلم يعطهم إلا عن طيب خواطر المسلمين. «فتح الباري» (٤٨٩/٧).

٩٠٥٤ — عن عمر بن الخطاب قال: أما والذي نفسي بيده، لولا أن أترك آخر الناس بَبَّانًا ليس لهم شيء، ما فتحت عليَّ قرية إلا قسمتها كما قسم النبي ﷺ خيبر، ولكني أتركها خزانة لهم يقتسمونها.
صحيح: رواه البخاري في المغازي (٤٢٣٥) عن سعيد بن أبي مريم، أخبرنا محمد بن جعفر، أخبرني زيد (هو ابن أسلم) عن أبيه، أنه سمع عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه قال: فذكره.
قوله: «بَبَّانًا» هو المعدم الذي لا شيء له.

9054 — ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb said: “By the One in whose hand is my soul, were it not that the later generations would otherwise be left destitute with nothing, I would distribute every territory conquered during my rule just as the Prophet ﷺ distributed Khaybar. Instead, I leave it as a common treasury for them, from which they may receive their shares.”
Authentic: Al-Bukhārī related it in al-Maghāzī (4235) from Saʿīd ibn Abī Maryam, from Muḥammad ibn Jaʿfar, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father, who heard ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb, may Allah be pleased with him.
The word babbānan refers to destitute people who possess nothing.

٩٠٥٥ — عن عبد الرحمن بن غنم قال: رابطنا مدينة قنسرين مع شرحبيل بن السمط. فلما فتحها أصاب فيها غنمًا وبقرًا، فقسم فينا طائفة منها، وجعل بقيتها في المغنم.
فلقيت معاذ بن جبل فحدثته، فقال معاذ: غزونا مع رسول الله ﷺ خيبر، فأصبنا فيها غنمًا، فقسم فينا رسول الله ﷺ طائفة، وجعل بقيتها في المغنم.
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٢٧٠٧) – ومن طريقه البيهقي (٩/٦٠) – عن محمد بن المصفى، حدثنا محمد بن المبارك، عن يحيى بن حمزة، حدثنا أبو عبد العزيز – شيخ من أهل الأردن – عن عبادة بن نسي، عن عبد الرحمن بن غنم فذكره.

9055 — ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ghanm reported: We were stationed on the frontier at the city of Qinnasrīn with Shuraḥbīl ibn al-Simṭ. When he conquered it, he acquired sheep and cattle. He distributed some of them among us and placed the remainder with the general spoils.
I later met Muʿādh ibn Jabal and told him about it. Muʿādh said: “We campaigned at Khaybar with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and acquired sheep there. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ distributed some of them among us and placed the remainder with the general spoils.”
Good: Abū Dāwūd related it (2707)—and through him al-Bayhaqī (9/60)—from Muḥammad ibn al-Muṣaffā, from Muḥammad ibn al-Mubārak, from Yaḥyā ibn Ḥamzah, from Abū ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, from ʿUbādah ibn Nusayy, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ghanm.

٩٠٥٦ — عن سهل بن أبي حثمة قال: قسم رسول الله ﷺ خيبر نصفين: نصفًا لنوائبه وحاجته، ونصفًا بين المسلمين، قسمها بينهم على ثمانية عشر سهمًا.
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٣٠١٠) عن الربيع بن سليمان المؤذن، حدثنا أسد بن موسى، حدثنا يحيى بن زكريا، حدثني سفيان، عن يحيى بن سعيد، عن بشير بن يسار، عن سهل بن أبي حثمة فذكره.

9056 — Sahl ibn Abī Ḥathmah reported: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ divided Khaybar into two halves: one half was reserved for emergencies and other needs, while the other half was distributed among the Muslims in eighteen shares.

٩٠٥٧ — عن أم المؤمنين عائشة أن فاطمة عليها السلام بنت النبي ﷺ أرسلت إلى أبي بكر تسأله ميراثها من رسول الله ﷺ مما أفاء الله عليه بالمدينة وفدك، وما بقي من خمس خيبر.
فقال أبو بكر: إن رسول الله ﷺ قال: «لَا نُورَثُ، مَا تَرَكْنَا صَدَقَةٌ، إِنَّمَا يَأْكُلُ آلُ مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ مِنْ هَذَا الْمَالِ». وإني والله لا أغير شيئًا من صدقة رسول الله ﷺ عن حالها التي كانت عليها في عهد رسول الله ﷺ، ولأعملن فيها بما عمل به رسول الله ﷺ.
فأبى أبو بكر أن يدفع إلى فاطمة منها شيئًا، فوجدت فاطمة على أبي بكر في ذلك، فهجرته فلم تكلمه حتى توفيت. وعاشت بعد النبي ﷺ ستة أشهر.
فلما توفيت دفنها زوجها علي ليلًا، ولم يؤذن بها أبا بكر، وصلى عليها.
وكان لعلي من الناس وجه حياة فاطمة. فلما توفيت استنكر علي وجوه الناس، فالتمس مصالحة أبي بكر ومبايعته، ولم يكن يبايع تلك الأشهر.

9057 — The Mother of the Believers ʿĀʾishah reported that Fāṭimah, peace be upon her, the daughter of the Prophet ﷺ, sent a request to Abū Bakr for her inheritance from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: from the property Allah had granted him as fayʾ in Madinah and Fadak, and from what remained of the one-fifth of Khaybar.
Abū Bakr replied: “The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: ‘We prophets are not inherited from; whatever we leave is charity. The family of Muḥammad ﷺ may only receive their sustenance from this property.’ By Allah, I shall not alter any part of the charity of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ from the condition in which it existed during his lifetime. I shall administer it exactly as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ administered it.”
Abū Bakr therefore declined to give Fāṭimah any of that property. Fāṭimah became displeased with Abū Bakr concerning the matter and withdrew from speaking to him until she died. She lived for six months after the Prophet ﷺ.
When she died, her husband ʿAlī buried her at night without informing Abū Bakr of her death, and ʿAlī performed the funeral prayer over her.
ʿAlī held a position of respect among the people during Fāṭimah’s lifetime. After she died, he perceived a change in the people’s attitude toward him, so he sought reconciliation with Abū Bakr and wished to pledge allegiance to him. He had not given the pledge during those months.
He sent word to Abū Bakr: “Come to us, but let no one accompany you,” because he disliked the prospect of ʿUmar being present.
ʿUmar said, “By Allah, you must not enter upon them alone.”
Abū Bakr replied, “What could they possibly do to me? By Allah, I shall go to them.”
Abū Bakr entered upon them. ʿAlī pronounced the testimony of faith and said:
“We recognise your virtue and what Allah has granted you. We do not begrudge you any good that Allah has brought to you. However, you acted independently of us concerning the matter of leadership, while we believed that our kinship with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entitled us to some consideration.”
Abū Bakr’s eyes overflowed with tears.
When Abū Bakr spoke, he said:
“By the One in whose hand is my soul, maintaining ties with the relatives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is dearer to me than maintaining ties with my own relatives.
“As for the disagreement that arose between us concerning this property, I have not fallen short in pursuing what is right. I have not omitted anything that I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do with it; I have done exactly as he did.”
ʿAlī said to Abū Bakr, “I shall meet you this afternoon to give the pledge of allegiance.”
After Abū Bakr performed the noon prayer, he ascended the pulpit, pronounced the testimony of faith, mentioned ʿAlī’s situation and his delay in giving the pledge, and related the explanation ʿAlī had given him. He then asked Allah for forgiveness.
ʿAlī then pronounced the testimony of faith, affirmed the great rights of Abū Bakr and explained that his conduct had not arisen from jealousy toward Abū Bakr or from any denial of the distinction Allah had granted him. Rather, he said:
“We believed that we were entitled to some consideration in this matter, but it was decided without consulting us, and this caused us to feel hurt.”
The Muslims were pleased by this and said, “You have acted correctly.” The Muslims then drew close to ʿAlī again after he returned to the recognised course of unity and reconciliation.
Agreed upon: Related by al-Bukhārī (4240, 4241) and Muslim (1759:52).

ʿAlī held a position of respect among the people during Fāṭimah’s lifetime. After she died, he perceived a change in the people’s attitude toward him, so he sought reconciliation with Abū Bakr and wished to pledge allegiance to him. He had not given the pledge during those months.
He sent word to Abū Bakr: “Come to us, but let no one accompany you,” because he disliked the prospect of ʿUmar being present.
ʿUmar said, “By Allah, you must not enter upon them alone.”
Abū Bakr replied, “What could they possibly do to me? By Allah, I shall go to them.”
Abū Bakr entered upon them. ʿAlī pronounced the testimony of faith and said:
“We recognise your virtue and what Allah has granted you. We do not begrudge you any good that Allah has brought to you. However, you acted independently of us concerning the matter of leadership, while we believed that our kinship with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entitled us to some consideration.”
Abū Bakr’s eyes overflowed with tears.
When Abū Bakr spoke, he said:
“By the One in whose hand is my soul, maintaining ties with the relatives of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is dearer to me than maintaining ties with my own relatives.
“As for the disagreement that arose between us concerning this property, I have not fallen short in pursuing what is right. I have not omitted anything that I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ do with it; I have done exactly as he did.”
ʿAlī said to Abū Bakr, “I shall meet you this afternoon to give the pledge of allegiance.”
After Abū Bakr performed the noon prayer, he ascended the pulpit, pronounced the testimony of faith, mentioned ʿAlī’s situation and his delay in giving the pledge, and related the explanation ʿAlī had given him. He then asked Allah for forgiveness.
ʿAlī then pronounced the testimony of faith, affirmed the great rights of Abū Bakr and explained that his conduct had not arisen from jealousy toward Abū Bakr or from any denial of the distinction Allah had granted him. Rather, he said:
“We believed that we were entitled to some consideration in this matter, but it was decided without consulting us, and this caused us to feel hurt.”
The Muslims were pleased by this and said, “You have acted correctly.” The Muslims then drew close to ʿAlī again after he returned to the recognised course of unity and reconciliation.

٩٠٥٨ — عن أبي موسى قال: بلغنا مخرج النبي ﷺ ونحن باليمن، فخرجنا مهاجرين إليه: أنا وأخوان لي، أنا أصغرهم؛ أحدهما أبو بردة، والآخر أبو رهم، إما قال: بضع، وإما قال: في ثلاثة وخمسين، أو اثنين وخمسين رجلًا من قومي.
فركبنا سفينة، فألقتنا سفينتنا إلى النجاشي بالحبشة، فوافقنا جعفر بن أبي طالب، فأقمنا معه حتى قدمنا جميعًا، فوافقنا النبي ﷺ حين افتتح خيبر.
وكان أناس من الناس يقولون لنا، يعني لأهل السفينة: سبقناكم بالهجرة.
ودخلت أسماء بنت عميس، وهي ممن قدم معنا، على حفصة زوج النبي ﷺ زائرة، وقد كانت هاجرت إلى النجاشي فيمن هاجر.
فدخل عمر على حفصة وأسماء عندها، فقال عمر حين رأى أسماء: من هذه؟ قالت: أسماء بنت عميس.
قال عمر: الحبشية هذه؟ البحرية هذه؟ قالت أسماء: نعم.
قال: سبقناكم بالهجرة، فنحن أحق برسول الله ﷺ منكم.
فغضبت وقالت: كلا والله! كنتم مع رسول الله ﷺ يطعم جائعكم، ويعظ جاهلكم، وكنا في دار، أو في أرض، البعداء البغضاء بالحبشة، وذلك في الله وفي رسوله ﷺ.
وأيم الله، لا أطعم طعامًا ولا أشرب شرابًا حتى أذكر ما قلت لرسول الله ﷺ. ونحن كنا نؤذى ونخاف، وسأذكر ذلك للنبي ﷺ وأسأله. والله لا أكذب ولا أزيغ ولا أزيد عليه.
فلما جاء النبي ﷺ قالت: يا نبي الله، إن عمر قال كذا وكذا.
قال: «فَمَا قُلْتِ لَهُ؟». قالت: قلت له كذا وكذا.
قال: «لَيْسَ بِأَحَقَّ بِي مِنْكُمْ؛ وَلَهُ وَلِأَصْحَابِهِ هِجْرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ، وَلَكُمْ أَنْتُمْ، أَهْلَ السَّفِينَةِ، هِجْرَتَانِ».
قالت: فلقد رأيت أبا موسى وأصحاب السفينة يأتونني أرسالًا، يسألونني عن هذا الحديث. ما من الدنيا شيء هم به أفرح، ولا أعظم في أنفسهم، مما قال لهم النبي ﷺ.
قال أبو بردة: قالت أسماء: فلقد رأيت أبا موسى وإنه ليستعيد هذا الحديث مني.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري في المغازي (٤٢٣١،٤٢٣٠) ومسلم في فضائل الصحابة (١٦٩:٢٥٠٣،٢٥٠٢) كلاهما عن محمد بن العلاء، حدثنا أبو أسامة، حدثني بريد بن عبد الله عن أبي بردة، عن أبي موسى قال: فذكره.

9058 — Abū Mūsā reported: News of the Prophet’s ﷺ migration reached us while we were in Yemen, so we set out to emigrate to him. I travelled with two of my brothers, of whom I was the youngest: one was Abū Burdah and the other Abū Ruhm. We were accompanied by either a little over fifty—or specifically fifty-three or fifty-two—men from my tribe.
We boarded a ship, but it carried us to the Negus in Abyssinia. There we met Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib and remained with him until we all travelled together and reached the Prophet ﷺ at the time he conquered Khaybar.
Some people used to say to us—the people of the ship—“We preceded you in emigration.”
Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays, who had arrived with us, visited Ḥafṣah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ. Asmāʾ had been among those who emigrated to the Negus.
ʿUmar entered upon Ḥafṣah while Asmāʾ was with her. When he saw Asmāʾ, he asked, “Who is this?”
Ḥafṣah replied, “Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays.”
ʿUmar asked, “Is this the Abyssinian woman—the woman who travelled by sea?”
Asmāʾ replied, “Yes.”
ʿUmar said, “We preceded you in emigration, so we have a greater claim to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than you do.”
Asmāʾ became angry and replied, “No, by Allah! You were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: he fed those of you who were hungry and instructed those of you who were ignorant. Meanwhile, we lived in the distant and hostile land of Abyssinia—and we endured that for the sake of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.”
“By Allah, I shall neither eat nor drink until I tell the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what you have said. We were persecuted and lived in fear. I shall mention this to the Prophet ﷺ and ask him about it. By Allah, I shall neither lie, distort your words nor add anything to them.”
When the Prophet ﷺ arrived, Asmāʾ said, “Prophet of Allah, ʿUmar said such-and-such.”
He asked: “What did you say to him?”
She related her response.
The Prophet ﷺ said: “He has no greater claim to me than you do. He and his companions have one emigration, while you—the people of the ship—have two emigrations.”
Asmāʾ said: “I saw Abū Mūsā and the people of the ship coming to me in successive groups to ask about this report. Nothing in the world brought them greater happiness or was more significant to them than what the Prophet ﷺ had said about them.”
Abū Burdah reported that Asmāʾ said: “I saw Abū Mūsā repeatedly asking me to relate this report to him again.”
Agreed upon: Al-Bukhārī related it in al-Maghāzī (4230, 4231) and Muslim in Faḍāʾil al-Ṣaḥābah (2502, 2503:169), both from Muḥammad ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, from Abū Usāmah, from Burayd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū Burdah, from Abū Mūsā.

قال: «لَيْسَ بِأَحَقَّ بِي مِنْكُمْ؛ وَلَهُ وَلِأَصْحَابِهِ هِجْرَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ، وَلَكُمْ أَنْتُمْ، أَهْلَ السَّفِينَةِ، هِجْرَتَانِ».
قالت: فلقد رأيت أبا موسى وأصحاب السفينة يأتونني أرسالًا، يسألونني عن هذا الحديث. ما من الدنيا شيء هم به أفرح، ولا أعظم في أنفسهم، مما قال لهم النبي ﷺ.
قال أبو بردة: قالت أسماء: فلقد رأيت أبا موسى وإنه ليستعيد هذا الحديث مني.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري في المغازي (٤٢٣١،٤٢٣٠) ومسلم في فضائل الصحابة (١٦٩:٢٥٠٣،٢٥٠٢) كلاهما عن محمد بن العلاء، حدثنا أبو أسامة، حدثني بريد بن عبد الله عن أبي بردة، عن أبي موسى قال: فذكره.
9058 — Abū Mūsā reported: News of the Prophet’s ﷺ migration reached us while we were in Yemen, so we set out to emigrate to him. I travelled with two of my brothers, of whom I was the youngest: one was Abū Burdah and the other Abū Ruhm. We were accompanied by either a little over fifty—or specifically fifty-three or fifty-two—men from my tribe.
We boarded a ship, but it carried us to the Negus in Abyssinia. There we met Jaʿfar ibn Abī Ṭālib and remained with him until we all travelled together and reached the Prophet ﷺ at the time he conquered Khaybar.
Some people used to say to us—the people of the ship—“We preceded you in emigration.”
Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays, who had arrived with us, visited Ḥafṣah, the wife of the Prophet ﷺ. Asmāʾ had been among those who emigrated to the Negus.
ʿUmar entered upon Ḥafṣah while Asmāʾ was with her. When he saw Asmāʾ, he asked, “Who is this?”
Ḥafṣah replied, “Asmāʾ bint ʿUmays.”
ʿUmar asked, “Is this the Abyssinian woman—the woman who travelled by sea?”
Asmāʾ replied, “Yes.”
ʿUmar said, “We preceded you in emigration, so we have a greater claim to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ than you do.”
Asmāʾ became angry and replied, “No, by Allah! You were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: he fed those of you who were hungry and instructed those of you who were ignorant. Meanwhile, we lived in the distant and hostile land of Abyssinia—and we endured that for the sake of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.”
“By Allah, I shall neither eat nor drink until I tell the Messenger of Allah ﷺ what you have said. We were persecuted and lived in fear. I shall mention this to the Prophet ﷺ and ask him about it. By Allah, I shall neither lie, distort your words nor add anything to them.”
When the Prophet ﷺ arrived, Asmāʾ said, “Prophet of Allah, ʿUmar said such-and-such.”
He asked: “What did you say to him?”
She related her response.
The Prophet ﷺ said: “He has no greater claim to me than you do. He and his companions have one emigration, while you—the people of the ship—have two emigrations.”
Asmāʾ said: “I saw Abū Mūsā and the people of the ship coming to me in successive groups to ask about this report. Nothing in the world brought them greater happiness or was more significant to them than what the Prophet ﷺ had said about them.”
Abū Burdah reported that Asmāʾ said: “I saw Abū Mūsā repeatedly asking me to relate this report to him again.”
Agreed upon: Al-Bukhārī related it in al-Maghāzī (4230, 4231) and Muslim in Faḍāʾil al-Ṣaḥābah (2502, 2503:169), both from Muḥammad ibn al-ʿAlāʾ, from Abū Usāmah, from Burayd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Abū Burdah, from Abū Mūsā.

٩٠٥٩ — عن أبي هريرة قال: أتيت رسول الله ﷺ وهو بخيبر بعدما افتتحوها، فقلت: يا رسول الله، أسهم لي.
فقال بعض بني سعيد بن العاص: لا تسهم له يا رسول الله.
فقال أبو هريرة: هذا قاتل ابن قوقل.
فقال ابن سعيد بن العاص: واعجبًا لوَبْرٍ تدلى علينا من قدوم ضأن، ينعى عليَّ قتل رجل مسلم أكرمه الله على يدي، ولم يهني على يديه!
قال: فلا أدري أسهم له أم لم يسهم له.
صحيح: رواه البخاري في الجهاد والسير (٢٨٢٧) عن الحميدي، حدثنا سفيان، حدثنا الزهري، قال: أخبرني عنبسة بن سعيد، عن أبي هريرة قال: فذكره.
«ابن قوقل» اسمه النعمان بن مالك بن ثعلبة، وقوقل لقب ثعلبة، استشهد يوم أحد.
و«بعض بني سعيد بن العاص» هو أبان بن سعيد.
قوله: «لوبر تدلى علينا من قدوم ضأن»: الوبر دابة صغيرة كالسنور، وحشية. أراد أبان بهذا تحقير أبي هريرة.
و«تدلى» كأنه يقول: تهجم علينا بغتة. و«قدوم ضأن» أي طرف ضأن. وأما ضأن فقيل: هو رأس الجبل؛ لأنه في الغالب مرعى الغنم، وقيل: هو بغير همز، جبل لدوس قوم أبي هريرة. وجاء في رواية باللام: «ضال» بدل النون، ومعناه السدر البري.
قوله: «أكرمه الله على يدي» يعني أن النعمان بن مالك بن قوقل استشهد بيد أبان، فأكرمه الله بالشهادة، ولم يقتل أبان على كفره فيدخل النار، وهو المراد بالإهانة، بل عاش أبان حتى تاب وأسلم.
قوله: «لا أدري أسهم له أم لم يسهم له»: القائل هو ابن عيينة.

9059 — Abū Hurayrah reported: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Khaybar after its conquest and said, “Messenger of Allah, allot me a share.”
A man from the family of Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ said, “Do not allot him a share, Messenger of Allah.”
Abū Hurayrah said, “This is the man who killed Ibn Qawqal.”
The son of Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ replied, “How astonishing that a small wild animal should descend upon us from the summit of Ḍaʾn and reproach me for killing a Muslim man whom Allah honoured at my hands, while He did not disgrace me at his hands!”
The narrator said: I do not know whether the Prophet ﷺ allotted Abū Hurayrah a share or not.
Authentic: Al-Bukhārī related it in al-Jihād wa-l-Siyar (2827) from al-Ḥumaydī, from Sufyān, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿAnbasah ibn Saʿīd, from Abū Hurayrah.
“Ibn Qawqal” was al-Nuʿmān ibn Mālik ibn Thaʿlabah. Qawqal was a title given to Thaʿlabah. Al-Nuʿmān was martyred at Uḥud.
The man described as “one of the family of Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ” was Abān ibn Saʿīd.
His words, “a small wild animal descended upon us from the summit of Ḍaʾn,” use wabr—a small wild animal resembling a cat—as a derogatory reference to Abū Hurayrah.
“Descended upon us” means that he suddenly appeared among them. “The summit of Ḍaʾn” means its extremity. It has been said that Ḍaʾn refers to a mountain summit, since such places are commonly grazing grounds for sheep. It has also been said that Ḍān, without a hamzah, was a mountain belonging to Daws, the tribe of Abū Hurayrah. Another narration reads ḍāl, with an l instead of an n, referring to a wild lote tree.
The statement, “Allah honoured him at my hands,” means that al-Nuʿmān ibn Mālik ibn Qawqal was killed by Abān and thereby honoured by Allah with martyrdom. Abān himself was not killed while still a disbeliever—which would have disgraced him by causing him to enter the Fire—but lived until he repented and embraced Islam.
The speaker who said, “I do not know whether he allotted him a share,” was Ibn ʿUyaynah.

٩٠٦٠ — عن أبي هريرة أن رسول الله ﷺ بعث أبان بن سعيد بن العاص على سرية من المدينة قِبَل نجد. فقدم أبان بن سعيد وأصحابه على رسول الله ﷺ بخيبر بعدما فتحها، وإن حُزُم خيلهم ليف.
فقال أبان: اقسم لنا يا رسول الله.
قال أبو هريرة: فقلت: لا تقسم لهم يا رسول الله.
فقال أبان: أنت بها يا وَبْر، تحدر علينا من رأس ضال!
فقال النبي ﷺ: «اجْلِسْ يَا أَبَانُ». ولم يقسم لهم رسول الله ﷺ.
حسن: رواه أبو داود (٢٧٢٣)، وسعيد بن منصور في «سننه» (٢٨٥/٢).

9060 — Abū Hurayrah reported that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Abān ibn Saʿīd ibn al-ʿĀṣ as commander of a detachment from Madinah toward Najd. Abān and his companions arrived before the Messenger of Allah ﷺ at Khaybar after its conquest, with their horses’ girths made of palm fibre.
Abān said, “Messenger of Allah, allot us shares.”
Abū Hurayrah said, “Messenger of Allah, do not allot them shares.”
Abān replied, “You again, little wild animal, descending upon us from the summit of Ḍāl!”
The Prophet ﷺ said: “Sit down, Abān.” The Messenger of Allah ﷺ did not allot them shares.
Good: Related by Abū Dāwūd (2723) and Saʿīd ibn Manṣūr in his Sunan (2/285).

٩٠٦١ — عن عمير مولى آبي اللحم قال: شهدت خيبر مع سادتي، فكلموا فيَّ رسول الله ﷺ، وكلموه أني مملوك.
قال: فأمر بي، فقُلِّدت السيف، فإذا أنا أجره. فأمر لي بشيء من خُرْثِيِّ المتاع.
وعرضت عليه رقية كنت أرقي بها المجانين، فأمرني بطرح بعضها وحبس بعضها.
وفي رواية: وأعطاني من خُرْثِيِّ المتاع، ولم يسهم لي.
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٢٧٣٠)، والترمذي (١٥٥٧)، وابن ماجه (٢٨٥٥)، والنسائي في «الكبرى» (٧٤٩٣).
وقوله: «خُرْثِيُّ المتاع»: أثاث البيت كالقدر ونحوه.

english_source:
9061 — ʿUmayr, the freedman of Ābī al-Laḥm, reported: I witnessed Khaybar with my masters. They spoke to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ concerning me and informed him that I was enslaved.
He ordered that I be equipped with a sword, but it was so long for me that I dragged it along the ground. He then ordered that I be given some miscellaneous household goods.
I also presented to him an incantation that I used when treating those afflicted with insanity. He instructed me to omit part of it and retain the remainder.
Another narration states: “He gave me some miscellaneous household goods but did not allot me a formal share.”
Authentic: Related by Abū Dāwūd (2730), al-Tirmidhī (1557), Ibn Mājah (2855) and al-Nasāʾī in al-Sunan al-Kubrā (7493).
“Miscellaneous household goods” refers to ordinary domestic items such as cooking pots and similar objects.

٩٠٦٢ — عن أبي ليلى قال: شهدت مع رسول الله ﷺ فتح خيبر. فلما انهزموا وقعنا في رحالهم، فأخذ الناس ما وجدوا من خُرْثِيٍّ، فلم يكن أسرع من أن فارت القدور.
قال: فأمر رسول الله ﷺ بالقدور فأكفئت، وقسم بيننا، فجعل لكل عشرة شاة.
صحيح: رواه أحمد (١٩٠٥٨)، والدارمي (٢٥١٣)، والحاكم (١٣٤/٢)، واللفظ لأحمد.

english_source:
9062 — Abū Laylā reported: I witnessed the conquest of Khaybar with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. When its people were defeated, we entered their encampment, and the Muslims took whatever ordinary goods they found. Before long, the cooking pots began to boil.
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ ordered that the pots be overturned. He then distributed the animals among us, allotting one sheep to every ten people.
Authentic: Related by Aḥmad (19058), al-Dārimī (2513) and al-Ḥākim (2/134). The wording is that of Aḥmad.

٩٠٦٣ — عن ثابت بن الحارث الأنصاري قال: قسم رسول الله ﷺ يوم خيبر لسهلة بنت عاصم بن عدي، ولابنة لها وُلدت.
حسن: رواه الطبراني في «الكبير» (٧٥/٢).
وقد ثبت أيضًا في صحيح مسلم (١٨١٢) أن النبي ﷺ أعطى النساء اللاتي كن يداوين الجرحى من الغنيمة، أما السهم فلم يضرب لهن.

english_source:
9063 — Thābit ibn al-Ḥārith al-Anṣārī reported: On the day of Khaybar, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ gave something from the spoils to Sahlah bint ʿĀṣim ibn ʿAdī and to a daughter who had been born to her.
Good: Related by al-Ṭabarānī in al-Muʿjam al-Kabīr (2/75).
It is also established in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim (1812) that the Prophet ﷺ gave something from the spoils to the women who treated the wounded, although he did not assign them formal shares.

٩٠٦٤ — عن عبد الله بن مغفل قال: كنا محاصرين قصر خيبر، فرمى إنسان بجراب فيه شحم، فنزوت لآخذه، فالتفت فإذا النبي ﷺ، فاستحييت منه.
وفي لفظ: فالتفت فإذا رسول الله ﷺ مبتسمًا.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري في فرض الخمس (٣١٥٣)، ومسلم في الجهاد والسير (١٧٧٢) كلاهما من حديث حميد بن هلال، عن عبد الله بن مغفل فذكره.

٩٠٦٦ — عن محمد بن أبي المجالد قال: بعثني أهل المسجد إلى ابن أبي أوفى أسأله عما صنع النبي ﷺ في طعام خيبر.
فأتيته، فسألته عن ذلك، وقلت: هل خمّسه؟ قال: لا، كان أقل من ذلك، وكان أحدنا إذا أراد منه شيئًا أخذ حاجته.
وفي لفظ: فكان الرجل يجيء، فيأخذ منه مقدار ما يكفيه، ثم ينصرف.
صحيح: رواه أبو داود (٢٧٠٤) وأحمد (١٩١٢٤) وصحّحه الحاكم (٢/١٢٦) من طريقين عن أبي إسحاق الشيباني، عن محمد بن أبي المجالد فذكره.

9066 — Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Mujālid reported: The people of the mosque sent me to Ibn Abī Awfā to ask him what the Prophet ﷺ had done with the food acquired at Khaybar.
I went to him and asked, “Did he take one-fifth of it?”
He replied, “No, it was too insignificant for that. Whenever one of us needed some of it, he took what he required.”
Another wording states: “A man would come, take the amount sufficient for his needs and then leave.”
Authentic: Abū Dāwūd (2704) and Aḥmad (19124) related it, and al-Ḥākim authenticated it (2/126), through two routes from Abū Isḥāq al-Shaybānī, from Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Mujālid.

٩٠٦٧ — عن عائشة قالت: لما فتحت خيبر قلنا: الآن نشبع من التمر.

arabic_source:
٩٠٦٩ — عن أنس قال: لما قدم المهاجرون المدينة من مكة، وليس بأيديهم شيء، وكانت الأنصار أهل الأرض والعقار، فقاسمهم الأنصار على أن أعطوهم أنصاف ثمار أموالهم كل عام، ويكفوهم العمل والمؤونة.
وكانت أم أنس، وهي تدعى أم سليم، وكانت أم عبد الله بن أبي طلحة، وكان أخًا لأنس لأمه، قد أعطت رسول الله ﷺ عِذَاقًا لها، فأعطاهن رسول الله ﷺ أم أيمن، مولاته أم أسامة بن زيد.
قال ابن شهاب: فأخبرني أنس بن مالك أن النبي ﷺ لما فرغ من قتال أهل خيبر وانصرف إلى المدينة، رد المهاجرون إلى الأنصار منائحهم التي كانوا منحوهم من ثمارهم.
فرد النبي ﷺ إلى أم أنس عذاقها، وأعطى رسول الله ﷺ أم أيمن مكانهن من حائطه.
قال ابن شهاب: وكان من شأن أم أيمن، أم أسامة بن زيد، أنها كانت وصيفة لعبد الله بن عبد المطلب، وكانت من الحبشة.
فلما ولدت آمنة رسول الله ﷺ، بعدما توفي أبوه، كانت أم أيمن تحضنه حتى كبر رسول الله ﷺ، فأعتقها، ثم أنكحها زيد بن حارثة.
ثم توفيت بعدما توفي رسول الله ﷺ بخمسة أشهر.
متفق عليه: رواه البخاري في الهبة (٢٦٣٠) ومسلم في الجهاد والسير (٧٠:١٧٧١) كلاهما من طريق ابن وهب، أخبرني يونس، عن ابن شهاب، عن أنس بن مالك فذكره.
